en: Master Weifeng Jianlao came from the road of Shu. Early on, he and his senior brother Shitian were both chief disciples of Pō’ān;

they attained the eye within the phrase and wielded authority beyond the borders of their jurisdiction. He was as perilous as the high walls of Mount Jiange, standing ten thousand *zhang* tall and sheer;
he snatched away the "Ruyi" (Wish-Fulfilling) staff of Zitrong and cut off all currents. Having passed from Qingliang to Jiaoshan, he moved from Xuedou to Mount Mao.
Driven by the winds of karma, you are cast onto the peaks of the Five Summits; your past debts are difficult to evade. Alas, how can you withstand the apocalyptic fires of the Western Barbarians?
You all employ every manner of stratagem for this mere trifle, yet remain nothing but deluded and stubborn. A heap of rubble and debris, your *khakkhara* staffs still stand crosswise as before.
Amidst the chaotic labor of craftsmen, each of you must swallow his own diamond circle. Thus it was asked at the fifth assembly.

Answer: To raise this matter for discussion: he has undergone no small amount of scrutiny within the monastic community. A month prior to his passing into stillness, I selected these passages and compiled them for you as a subject.
Moreover, since he himself once wrote them freely with his own hand and willingly admitted their validity, it is utterly redundant to further cite others to bear witness.
Examining the matter closely, what relevance does this have? I fear only that, beneath the sandalwood forest, they will be copied and circulated from one to another.
How is it that one might casually cast [a thing] into the side of a wooden pit, merely seeking to avoid trouble and escape the outbreak of calamity?
Although this is so, how, after all, should this public case (gong'an) be resolved? Have you not seen the ancient saying:
"How can a mirage ever quench thirst? When can a painted cake satisfy hunger? I urge you not to plant thorns yourself; later..."

"Bringing disaster upon one's descendants by clinging to clothes. *Duh!* Written on the day of Renzi, the second lunar month of the Xinsi year of the Chunyou era, by the Daoist of Cangzhou, Cheng Gongsu (style name Xiying), while dwelling in seclusion at Xizhan Hall on the Xi River.

The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Fojian, Volume One:
The Record of Chan Master Fojian’s First Residence at Qingliang Chan Temple in Qingyuan Prefecture,
Compiled by Attendant Zonghui and Zhizhe.
On the twenty-eighth day of the third month in the thirteenth year of the Jiading era, the Master entered the monastery. Pointing to the triple gate, he said:
"The road is level and straight; the courtyard is struck and cleared. Four verticals and three horizontals—everyone knows these exist. But when the new Qingliang arrives here, what will he do?
He then entered the temple and looked at the plaque.
The Buddha Hall: you sit while I stand; a difference of inches and centimeters, beyond the reach of mouth or ear—this is precisely what we must deliberate upon.
What is it we deliberate? Joining palms at the triple gate and burning incense within the Buddha Hall.
Sitting upon the square measure of the hall—three before and three behind; today and tomorrow. Bodhidharma did not understand;
for nine years he faced the wall. Holding up the official decree: the patriarch’s nostrils, the patch-robed monk’s nostrils.
There are some nostrils; there are none at all. Why is it so? The official warrant is clear.
He held up the Dharma robe and said: "One who wears the pure robe speaks of the Dharmakāya Buddha; one who wears the robe of non-differentiation speaks of the Sambhogakāya Buddha;
one who wears the robe of non-conceptualization speaks of the Nirmāṇakāya Buddha. He then lifted the robe and asked: "What kind of robe is this?"
The eyes of the multitude cannot deceive him.
He points to the Dharma-seat: "The precious Sumeru throne is eighty-four thousand *yojanas* high; the Buddha’s body is eighty-four thousand *yojanas* tall.
You must manifest your own body to be like that throne before you can sit upon it. Now tell me, how will the new Qingliang [sit]?
Regarding the question of his height, he replied, "It is the same. He then ascended the seat and, holding up the incense, said:
"This single offering of incense is respectfully presented to extend the holy longevity of the present Emperor—ten thousand years! Ten thousand years! Ten thousand times ten thousand years!

May he govern with the Golden Wheel, may the Jade Branch flourish in fragrance, may the four seas submit to benevolence, and may the myriad nations bring tribute. Next, he held up the incense and said:
This one portion of incense is offered for the Chancellor and Commander-in-Chief, the Minister, as well as all the honored officials of the Prefecture and the Provincial Governor, the Langzhong.

We humbly pray that you may forever assist the enlightened sovereign and long abide in your positions of rank and emolument. Next, holding up the incense, he says: This one portion of incense is offered for Yangqi, the Eighth [Patriarch].
The Great Master Pō’ān, the Abbot of Zifú Chan Temple on Fèngshān Mountain in Ānjì Prefecture during the Shì era, burns incense in the brazier to repay the milk of the Dharma.
He then takes his seat (the questions and answers are not recorded) and says: "At Vulture Peak they spoke of the moon; at Caoxi they pointed to the moon.
Passed down from generation to generation, they have taken a tortoise and certified it as a soft-shelled turtle. Upādhyāya Fàn, you usually have a mouth wide open."
It has hung upon the wall, never once moved. Today, for no reason at all, I have entered this profession.
Since matters have come to this, I can do nothing but sift through them from east to west;

I cannot help but take up my many years of records and point out a few places where people have been deceived, to tell you all. This is simply so that Guo Da, Li Er, Deng Si, and Zhang San may understand.
In Jiangnan and the two Zhejiang provinces, it is cold in spring and hot in autumn. Nevertheless, even so, the Yellow River clears itself only once every three thousand years.
Again, Master Qian of Yongming was asked by a monk: "When Bodhidharma came from the West, what did he transmit? Qian said:
He handed over this strategy. The monk said, "In that case, there are dharmas outside the mind. Qian said, "There are no dharmas within the mind.
Later, Fojian commented: "Within the mind and outside the mind; with dharmas and without dharmas—those who have even slightly engaged in inquiry will understand."
It is simply as it was said: "He transmits a memorandum. But tell me, what does that memorandum say?
"None of the disciples of Confucius recognized it; the blue-eyed barbarian monk smiled and nodded his head. The Master commented:

"In general, when clearly discerning the past and present or deciding upon right and wrong, one must also be able to cut through nails and sever iron. When Fojian raises the matter in this way, [what follows]..."
Vague and indistinct; in the end, they are coarse and superficial. Thus, they miss the point within the "Cai" (策) character.
But tell me, what exactly does that "Cai" character say? *Shang Daren* (上大人), *Qiu Yiji* (丘乙己).
That evening, there was a small *sǎn* (informal discourse; the questions and answers are not recorded). He then said: "The Dharma has no fixed characteristics;

it becomes the school as it encounters conditions. Its function does not halt its momentum, responding and adapting as appropriate. Sometimes what seems good is not necessarily good; sometimes what seems evil is not necessarily evil.
To spray *īlāna* flowers within a sandalwood grove, or for an iron ox to manifest golden horns—let us set this aside for a moment. But as for acting according to the command:"
"How do you say it in a single phrase? "The razor-sharp blade never stirs; the skulls throughout the world are cold. Again, he raised the case:
Deshan addressed the assembly, saying, "Tonight’s small *cán* (private inquiry) will not involve answering questions. Anyone who asks a question shall receive thirty blows of the staff.
At that time, a monk stepped forward, and Deshan struck him immediately. The monk said, "I have not even asked a question; why do you strike me? Deshan said, "You..."
"Where is this man from? The monk replied, "From Silla. Deshan said, "Before he has even stepped onto the ship's railing, thirty blows are well-deserved for him.
The Master [Xuedou] comments: "Old Deshan’s backbone was as hard as iron; it could not be bent.
For no reason, he was carelessly wrapped up and brought down by this monk with a single piece of hemp cloth. Tell me, where does the crux lie?"
[The Master] ascends the hall. Those with eyes will discern and grasp it for themselves.
My thanks to the two classes of officials. One is one; two are two. A little Śākyamuni from the Eastern Land.
The Indian Hu Da Mo clapped his knee once and said: "The Bian jade and the black pearl have become stagnant wares.

On the occasion of the Buddha-Bathing Ceremony, he ascended the hall and said: "Today marks the eighth day of the fourth month again; throughout the monasteries of the world, they all bathe the Buddha.
At Qingliang, there is an edict that cannot be carried out, so we all follow the custom by splashing about in the mud. Yet, even as we splash about, within it there is nonetheless..."
This is a point of clarity. But tell me, what clarity is there? The bearded monk from the Western Heaven has no whiskers;
the Yellow-Faced Gautama has no crown bone. If you do not believe this, you shall verify it for yourselves shortly in the Buddha Hall.
Ascending the hall: On the fourteenth and fifteenth days, one is as base as mud; on the sixteenth and seventeenth, one is as precious as gold and jade.
To whom is this meaning clearly explained? In heaven and on earth, I alone know it.
Ascending the hall: Since arriving to reside at Qingliang Temple, it has been a hurried month. When there is leisure, there is plenty of it; when there is busyness, one is never finished.
Who would have known that this busyness and leisure are both entirely made of iron? The spirit Śūnyatā-nirmita smiles and nods his head;
Gavāmpati sticks out his tongue in long astonishment.

Ascending the hall, he said: "To mention one, one must not mention two. Letting this matter pass for now, on this auspicious morning, I respectfully wish that the administrators, the head monks, the elders, and the great assembly may each enjoy ten thousand blessings in your health and well-being. Looking upon you from the left, you are as pure as ice and frost."
Gazing to the right, they are like gold and like jade; the crane is white and the crow is black; the pine is straight and the thorn is crooked.
The mountain monk reflects upon this again and again: six times six is originally thirty-six.
Ascending the hall: Gaudama winked his eyes; Kāśyapa broke into a smile. This mountain monk, having heard this, bites down firmly on his teeth.
Ascending the hall: When a single leaf falls, the whole world turns autumnal; when a single speck of dust rises, the entire earth is gathered up.
A spark flies from the forging of iron in Silla and burns the big toe of Master Wang in the Arhat Temple at Mount Lu. King of the Temple at Qiji.
Unable to restrain his pain, he broke into a profuse sweat over his entire body. Rising, he said, "The kindness is too great to repay. This made the Water-Ox of Mount Mui laugh until he fell over.
Upon the conclusion of the retreat, he ascended the hall and said: "Within a single hair-tip, a lion appears; within ten billion hair-tips, ten billion lions appear."

Manifesting within a single hair-pore, he raised his staff and said: "Look! Look! All the Buddhas of the ten directions, the great Bodhisattvas, and those in training and beyond training—all are performing acts of self-indulgent Buddha-work upon the tip of this Qingliang staff, engaging in vast and unceasing debate.
Then, struck by a shout from the old man Vimalakīrti, they were immediately reduced to a state of confusion and dispersed. Returning to the East."
If you go east, he returns to the south; if you go west, he returns to the west; if you go north, he returns to the north.

Having returned to his native land, he dwells according to his station and attends to his original task. Do you people see him now? If you do not see him, listen as this staff recites another verse once more.
*Thump!* (A single strike).
Ascending the hall on the Mid-Autumn Festival: The ordinary moon is the Mid-Autumn moon; The Mid-Autumn moon is the ordinary moon.

Upon closer inspection, it is truly just ordinary; Yet to say it is ordinary is already to treat it as something else. Something else! Something else! There is nothing that can be compared to it; How am I to describe it?

Ascending the hall on the auspicious anniversary of the Emperor’s birthday: "Clouds follow the dragon; wind follows the tiger. When the Sage appears, all things behold him. Xuefeng rolls three wooden balls;
the old Heshan strikes the drum with a single flavor. The waters of the sea surge in waves; Mount Sumeru performs a dance.
Why is this so? Heaven has no partiality; it assists only virtue.
When Head Seat Laofan arrived, he ascended the hall. A song of the warm spring, a stringless zither—its sound harmonizes with the six pitch-pipes, its resonance arranges the five musical notes.
The moon is cold and the wind is clear; the mountains are high and the waters are deep. Throughout the world, who knows this heart? After a long silence...
Looking back, he said: "Heh! Entering the hall:
How desolate is Qingliang Temple; its traditional style is truly pitiable. White clouds obscure the valley mouth; yellow leaves gather before the steps.

The patched robe is worn through, leaving the whole body cold; firewood has grown within the room, filling it with smoke. Who would have known that today’s affairs are no different from those of old?"

Throughout the year, the Abbot ascends the hall to express gratitude to the former and current stewards: The crane calls in the heavens; the fish leap in the deep abyss. They glide through the waves and swim beneath the moon, drifting on and on;
they ride upon the clouds and harness the winds, soaring and elegant. How timely! How timely! It cannot be fully illuminated by words. Thus it is commanded.
People always remember Old Nanquan. He ascended the hall and said:
"A guest comes from afar, bringing me a jade disc an inch across. Within it are four characters; no one recognizes these characters.
Xuedou only knows how to open his mouth, unaware that his tongue is too long. Qingliang, however, was not like this: "A guest comes from afar..."
Just as he was about to arrive, he left me a jade disc an inch across, within which are four characters that need not be further pointed out. Why?
Because the ancient seal script is perfectly clear.
Entering the hall: One must neither grasp nor let go. If this were so, Kāśyapa would have raised his hands in greeting; if it were not so, Ānanda would have been at fault.
[The Master] joined his palms. "Master Zhi is no ordinary monk.
He ascended the hall and said: "Where the Buddhas know, people do not know; this ignorance is most intimate. Where people understand, the Buddhas do not understand;
this lack of understanding is even more urgent. Now tell me, why is it so? When the rooster is cold, it climbs the tree; when the duck is cold, it enters the water."

The Buddha ascended the hall after attaining the Way. At midnight, the Old Barbarian saw the morning star; he blinded both his eyes for all his life, and even until now there has been nothing to grasp.
Every time it is raised, it brings forth a pang of sorrow. Nevertheless, one does not gain a single bit of wisdom without having experienced a single event.
When County Magistrate Wang arrived, the Master ascended the hall. He raised the public case of Attendant Wang’s visit to Linji, where they toured the monks’ hall.
The Master said: "Old Linji held the imperial decree in his hand; he could unfurl or roll it up as he pleased. Attendant Wang was like a bright mirror set upon its stand."
There is not a single point that can be concealed from him. As for what he said at the very end—“I took you for a mere worldly fellow”—how will you all deliberate upon this?
You must know that Fu Yue was no mere Fu Yue; do not mistake Zeng Shen for the "Lü Shen" (the rustic Shen).
Ascending the hall, he said: "The spring days linger on; the spring breeze sweeps vast and wide. A sharp-witted monk—when the point is made, he does not reach it.
Only Old Wang of East Village: how about him? After a long silence, he said: "Letting the ox graze on the grass by my stream."
The Opening of the Retreat: An Address to the Assembly. It is said that in antiquity it was remarked: "The ten directions gather together as one;
each and every one studies non-action (*wuwei*). This is the field for selecting a Buddha; with an empty mind, one returns having passed the examination.

If you say there is a "non-action" to be studied or a "Buddha" to be selected, then there will never be a time of passing the examination. If you say there is nothing to be selected and nothing to be studied, likewise there will never be a time of passing the examination.
"Ultimately, how is it? The flowers must bloom throughout the night; do not wait for the morning breeze to blow.
He ascended the hall and said: "Xuansha bit his big toe and has suffered the pain to this day. Shaodu drank in a kick from Master Ma."
He laughed heartily and would not stop. "The ten thousand bodhisattvas on Mount Qingliang—nowhere can they be found," he said.
Picking up his staff, he said, "So it was all along right here! He struck the ground with it once and said, "What a deception!"
Jie’an arrived; he ascended the hall and said: "Selling flour with bran, cooking rice with chaff. At the dead of night, they deceive the gods and shout to the ghosts.
If someone were to see them from a distance, they would simply have to cover their nose with their left hand. I, this mountain monk, burn aloeswood incense as an offering to them.
Why? Because those who are not karmic enemies do not meet."
Master Xie invited the assembly to enter the hall: "The grain is ripe, the beans are ripe; the porridge is sufficient, the rice is sufficient.
Looking up at the sky, both hands rub the belly. These words are entrusted to those monks who have already settled their affairs.

As for those whose mouths are red-hot, speaking of Chan, speaking of the Way, speaking of the mysterious and the wondrous, speaking of existence and non-existence, speaking of long and short—I dare not associate with them."
A comparison. Why? Because he resides in the Eastern Continent.

Having resigned from his official duties, he ascends the hall. In the sphere of action of a patch-robed monk, there is no fixed measure: one may grasp earth and turn it into gold, or grasp gold and turn it into earth.
Thus, at times he takes a step forward, where amidst a hundred affairs there is no room for evasion; at other times he takes a step back.
Enveloped in a patched robe and with head covered, one pays no heed at all. But what about when there is neither advancing nor retreating? Furthermore: the attendant strikes the drum;
the mountain monk ascends the hall; the assembly bows in greeting; the attendant burns incense—the fragrance of precepts, the fragrance of concentration, and the fragrance of wisdom.
May these clouds of incense pervade the entire Dharma-realm, making offerings to all Buddhas of the past, all Buddhas of the present, and all Buddhas of the future.

Furthermore, I look toward your great kindness and compassion. Raising his hand, he said: "Do not take my lack of formality to heart. I humbly pray that you will take care. He then ascended the hall and cited this:
A monk asked Yunmen, "What is it like when the trees are stripped bare and the leaves have fallen? Yunmen replied, "The golden wind reveals its essence."
This lame monk answered in such a way that he misled how many people! They took it not as an expression of the Buddha-dharma, but took it as a worldly convention;
they took it not as a worldly convention, but took it as an expression of the Buddha-dharma. If it were Qingliang, it would not be so.
If someone asked, "What is it like when the trees wither and the leaves fall? he would simply say to them, "The golden wind reveals its essence."
It must be like this before one attains it.

On the occasion of the Mid-Autumn Festival, he ascended the hall and said: "On the fifteenth day of the eighth month, the full moon faces the door; at midnight it is perfectly bright, yet at dawn it is no longer revealed."
If you grasp at the eye, the ear will surely go deaf; if you abandon the ear, the eye will surely go blind.

Have you not seen Old Changsha brandishing his claws and fangs? With a single kick, he toppled Little Śākyamuni. One might have thought him a great beast, but it turned out to be nothing more than a tiger.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Within heaven and earth, amidst the universe, there is a single treasure. Holding up his staff, he showed it to the assembly, saying, "Do you see it?
If you truly see it, you may enjoy its use at any time; it will simply be as it is, and you will never cause any alarm or stir.
If you do not see it, leave it where it is and do not touch it. He then leaned the staff against the wall.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Master Nanquan said, 'At eighteen, this monk understood how to make a living.
Master Zhaozhou said, 'At eighteen, this monk understood how to break up the family and scatter the household. Qingliang does not agree with them; at eighteen, this monk became a monk."
The eighteen great wandering monks leave one forest and enter another community; wherever they go, they do not pluck the horizontal grass nor grasp the upright grass.
At all times, they simply receive and enjoy what is already manifest.
Now, at forty-five, they remain exactly as they were before—dazed and bewildered, capable of nothing at all. Aha-ha! They are fit for the twilight years.
The clouds have returned but have not yet merged; the distant mountains stretch on endlessly, layer upon layer of azure.
Entering the hall: One winter, two winters—“you” and “I,” you and I. Smiling in secret behind one’s back, one utters empty falsehoods right to one’s face.
Though this is but ordinary food and drink, who knows there are worms within the rice? Have you not seen Nanquan say: "Last night there was a fine wind"?
He blew down a pine branch in front of the gate.
Entering the hall, he said: "To open one's mouth is an error; to keep it shut is to perish. Neither opening nor closing—it is a hundred thousand miles away.
Reaching this point, how can one transmit the message? Yesterday the director of the monastery prepared a vegetarian feast; whether monk or novice, all were satisfied. The lanterns are revealed."
The pillar is also satiated. Once satiated, one forgets a hundred hungers; everyone’s brows are fully unknotted.
On this day of great peace and no affairs, let us sing "Lalali. Good brother!
Ascending the hall: There are three hundred and sixty days in a year; the end of the twelfth month is the eve of the New Year. Last night the twelfth month came to an end;
the old year is departing. Today the new year has arrived. When dawn breaks, the gates shall be thrown wide open.

Waiting for the New Year, he did not appear at all. After hesitating for a long time, just as he was at a loss for what to do, suddenly a clever Great King appeared and said, "Elder! Elder! You must examine the calendar dates very carefully."
There is yet another intercalary month; I, this mountain monk, was pierced through by it and could not help but laugh aloud.
The past is already past, and the future is yet to come; that which is right now is called the present. But where does the present dwell?
These three sections are distinct, yet they are all gathered back into the primary category. (He strikes his staff once.)
Ascending the hall, he said: "If one were to discuss this matter, it is truly simple and easy to understand. Yet most of you create difficulties for yourselves and erect obstacles for yourselves.
Therefore, sometimes when I see you bowing and exchanging greetings on the eastern or western corridors, I simply lower my head to receive you.
In truth, there is nothing else; I only wish for you to recognize who this old monk is."
Tōkei of Saikawa served as a district official. If you had recognized him, you would have exchanged some local greetings with him and spoken some regional dialects.
For now, I shall not say that you recognize the Elder; rather, let each of you first know your own native place.
Do you know it? Mingzhou has six counties; Fenghua has eight districts.
Ascending the hall: Every year is a good year; every day is a good day. All know this auspicious matter well: today is the first day of the first month.

On this Lantern Festival, ascending the hall, people look at people and fire illuminates fire—without confusion or defilement, forgetting self and other. If you can understand it thus, [you have grasped it].
"I grant you the opportunity to see the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara face-to-face and receive his prediction of enlightenment.

Yet today, most of these ten groups of five are mostly sitting within the shadows of light; they move at every turn according to the heels of others. Then he called out in a loud voice, "Great assembly!
All, lift your heads! He spoke again, saying, "Do not believe me."
A general labor session for the assembly. First, dragging stones; second, carrying earth; three parts sweet, seven parts bitter.
Picking up the dustpan, they shoulder it upon their two shoulders; casting down the hoe, there is no place to be found. Oṃ bhaṇ phaṭ phaṭ śrī sulu.

The Buddha ascended the hall for the Nirvana assembly. This yellow-faced old fellow has five offenses of immeasurable gravity from two thousand years ago that, until this very day, not a single person has brought up. I, the young monk Qingliang, will not spare my verbal karma;
I shall point them out from the beginning so that everyone may know them together. From the very start, he did not abide by his own proper measure while in the Tuṣita Heaven, but manifested...

To be born in Jambudvīpa and yet commit such immeasurable transgressions as these— neither being fit to leap over the city walls at midnight nor going directly to the Snowy Mountains to undergo six years of asceticism,
exhausting every manner of display only to lose one's nostrils when facing the morning star— is truly a pity.
He was greatly startled and exclaimed in wonder, "How marvelous! All sentient beings possess the wisdom, virtue, and marks of a Tathāgata;

yet, because of deluded thoughts and attachments, they are unable to realize it. To act as if one were deceiving the world and hoodwinking the common people—this is the second measureless transgression.
Furthermore, it would be improper to have set out from the Bodhi tree, gone to the Deer Park, and arranged the Three Vehicles."

They divide the teachings into five categories, asserting existence and non-existence, sudden and gradual, partial and perfect, and uttering many idle words and long-winded speeches that defile the ears and eyes of others and bring calamity upon future generations; this is the third immeasurable transgression.
Finally, delivering a "non-combative" blow, he manifested *parinirvāṇa* beneath the twin śāla trees, stroking [the earth] with his hand...
He addressed the assembly, saying: "I am still speaking these words with my own mouth. Behold my body of purple-gold;
gaze upon it until you are fully satisfied, lest you later feel regret. If you say that I have entered parinirvāṇa, you are not my disciples. If you say that I have not entered parinirvāṇa..."
"Nor are they my disciples. To reach old age without knowing shame—this is the fourth immeasurable transgression.
There is yet a fifth immeasurable transgression. For a long while, enough! Enough! Do not count people until you have counted them all;
do not revile others until you have caught them. In a short while, descend from the seat. Together with the assembly, go to the Great Buddha Hall and burn a single stick of incense."
Brew a bowl of tea, prostrate three times universally, and let it all be covered over at once.

If you can cover it over, then the celestial Māras will fold their hands in submission, the heretics will turn their hearts toward the Way, Kāśyapa will raise his fists in greeting, and Ānanda will join his palms.
If you cannot cover it over, there will be new branches next year; the spring wind that disturbs us shall never cease.

Ascending the hall for the commencement of the summer retreat. Regarding the commencement of the summer retreat, the samādhi of presence before one, Puhua shaking his bell, and Old Lu treading the pestle—ascending the hall:
"The Way of the ancient sages is that this Dharma cannot be shown; words and signs are quiescent. What kind of statement is this?
Today, Qingliang extends his broad and long tongue. He then points and says: "This side is the incense burner; this side is..."
The Flower Vase. Do you understand? Buying for three coins, selling for two.

On the occasion of the Mid-Autumn Festival, he ascended the hall and cited Xuan Sha’s address to the assembly, which said: "I possess the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye, the wondrous mind of Nirvana."
Entrusting [the Dharma] to Mahākāśyapa was like pointing at the moon with words; Caoxi (Huineng) held up his whisk, which was like pointing at the moon with a finger.
Gushan stepped forward from the assembly and said, "The moon? Shanzhao said, "This monk has come to me seeking the moon.
Gushan shook his sleeves and returned to the assembly, saying, "He says I am coming to him seeking the moon. The Master said, "These two old cold fellows—how stubborn they are!"
An ox hide: where it is rotted, it is like tattered rags. Although each part has its own mechanism, alas, there is nowhere at all to stretch it out.
Thus, one simply lowers the head and returns in a daze, unaware that one has forgotten the path by which one came.
The Chief Seat Xie Yue and the Chief Seat Qiong brought the words of Yunchao to me. I ascended the hall and said: "One stillness cuts through all stillness;
one movement moves everything. Entering a field of weeds, he does not pick and choose; he takes whatever comes to hand and uses it.
Yesterday someone came from Sichuan, yet received news from Jiangdong, saying that Zhaozhou personally saw the old Nanquan. The radish of Zhenzhou."
Three catties in weight. Entering the hall:
When Kāśyapa Mātanga entered the Han, he stirred wind and waves upon level ground; when Bodhidharma came from the West, he further increased the calamities. This is so;
yet tell me, is the meaning of the Patriarchs the same as the meaning of the Teachings, or are they different? Monks of Sichuan are coarse; monks of Zhejiang are elegant.
Ascending the hall, he raised an example, saying: "Zhenjing addressed the assembly, saying: 'The Stone of Asceticism is enveloped in moss;
Peak of Thrown Pens is entangled by brambles. At the Arhat Temple, three novices are ordained each year; at Guizong Monastery, one drinks tea after the formal meditation session.
Great assembly, do you understand? This is the great divine mantra, this is the great illuminating mantra, this is the unsurpassed mantra, this is the unequaled mantra."
This mantra can eliminate all suffering; it is true and not false.

[The assembly] thanks the Karmadāna for the meal. The Head Seat (Śrāmaṇera) holds the whisk and ascends the hall. An ancient said: "That which is equal regarding food is also equal regarding all dharmas;
that which is equal regarding all dharmas is also equal regarding food. Thus, while the Karmadāna bestows material wealth, the Head Seat bestows the Dharma.
What is called the twofold giving of wealth and Dharma is equal and without distinction.

Since there is no distinction, it does not hinder one from taking the joy of dhyāna as flavor and the delight in the Dharma as bliss. Each according to what is appropriate, each attains enjoyment; each attains fulfillment.
There is no high or low, no limit or measure, and no such thing as equality or inequality. For what reason, then, do you say they are "shared"?
A precious vessel for food; the color of the rice differs. People vie with one another, marveling at those who have attained it.
An old acquaintance visits. Ascending the hall, the practitioners meet: you go west, I go east. The waters return to the vast sea;
the moon rises over the solitary peak. Letting loose the rats of the city to bite the tigers of the village—why is it so? Min and Shu.

In the same style, he ascended the hall upon his second tenure at Qingliang. He said: "The nose-rope has been pulled off; I have gone up to Meixi and lie across the thousand peaks—this is exactly what is appropriate.
Yet how could one escape the pull of karmic conditions? As before, I am yoked to the *qǐ* tree and made to pull the plow. Thus, he once again relished the old.

Amidst the mountain winds and moonlight, he once again tills his fields of old. He does not decline when his collar is torn and his hooves are pierced; how could he begrudge being dragged through mud and water?
Thus, the Old Teacher Wang said: "Since my youth, I have herded a single water buffalo. If I intend to herd it to the east of the stream," he would go there.

One cannot avoid infringing upon the water and grass belonging to another king’s domain. Even if one intends to graze toward the west of the stream, one still cannot avoid infringing upon the water and grass belonging to another king’s domain.
It would be better to simply accept things as they are, bit by bit; yet, even this "accepting some small portion" is ultimately not to be found.

Qingliang has a maxim: "If you have a branch, grasp it; if you have no branch, grasp the precedent. Since this is so, tell me: what is the principle of accepting things as they are, bit by bit? Yesterday...
The mountain departed yesterday; this morning he returns from the rear ridge. Entering the hall:
On the first day of the first month, the Lantern Festival, there is no oil, yet the lamps are not lit. Who understands this meaning? There is a moon that ascends the highest tier. Look, look!
The Lamp-Light Tathāgata dwells upon the eyelashes of all people, emitting light and manifesting his countenance. Behold him!
People did not gather it; it ran away and entered the kingdom of Great Stone. [The Master] pats the meditation seat and descends from it. Ascending the hall:
Last year’s plum, this year’s willow—their color and fragrance remain as they were. That they remain as they were is indeed so.

Why then is the southern branch facing the warmth while the northern branch suffers the cold? [The Master] pats the meditation seat and says: "Do not say that the spring breeze has two different natures."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The Buddha-dharma pervades all places—among all sentient beings and all lands.
There are worlds that perform the work of a Buddha through light; there are worlds that perform the work of a Buddha through fragrant food;

there are worlds that perform the work of a Buddha through silence, speechlessness, and non-explanation; and there are worlds that [perform the work of a Buddha] through dreams, illusions, reflections in a mirror, and water..."
The moon in the sky, a mirage in the heat, and the echo of a shout—through such metaphors, the Buddha performs his work.
Therefore, the true essence of the teaching in this land is pure within sound and hearing. (He strikes the staff once. "It is not only Avalokiteśvara who realizes it from within;
I too have realized it through this. (He strikes again. "To call a bell a jar!"
Ascending the Hall upon Leaving the Monastery: To remain, there is nothing to be said; to depart, there is likewise nothing to be said.
Wearing an eight-holed cloth robe, the Vajra chews raw iron.
*Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Fojian of Jiaoshan Pujisi in Zhenjiang Prefecture*
Compiled by the Attendant Jueyuan.
Three Gates. Gate One: The Buddha Hall. Seeing it at once: kicking over the water pitcher and shaking the door panels.
"In the Buddha Hall, you do not recognize me; I do not recognize you. Meeting on a narrow path, your forehead strikes the ground.
When the benevolent see this, they call it benevolence; when the wise see this, they call it wisdom."
The Abbot held his staff horizontally and said, "I, this mountain monk, act in this way for those of middling or inferior capacity.
But what if a person of superior capacity comes? [He] struck the ground with the staff and said, 'Thirty years hence.'"

Having ascended the seat and finished the prayers for the Emperor (the question-and-answer portion is not recorded), he then said: "Those who rest their heads on stones and rinse their mouths in mountain streams should be called up and struck.
Those who block the streets and cut across the lanes should also receive a blow behind the head.

Only when the ignorant have attained clarity, the obstructed have found passage, the seated have risen, and the wandering have arrived, may one be permitted to cross the gate of Jiaoshan, ascend the hall of Jiaoshan, enter the chamber of Jiaoshan, and behold [the Buddha]."
Jiaoshan: "If you see, you have seen; then Jiaoshan will slowly speak his words to you.
Why? The long river flows without end; the pine dew drips without ceasing. Again, he raised an old case: A monk asked Yunmen, "Is it true that the Buddha-dharma is like the moon in the water?
Yunmen said, "In the clear waves, there is no path through. The Master said: "This monk was caught in the light and shadow."
"Backstreet walker! Yunmen rolled into a patch of weeds, and even until today he has been unable to turn himself around.
Now tell me, where does the crux lie in Jiaoshan’s critique like this? [He lets out a shout]—and descends from the seat."
That evening’s informal discourse (*xiaochan*): A single word cuts it off—throughout ten thousand ages, all is dark and vast.
When the thread is let loose, the preceding waves and following billows clamor and chatter. Sometimes it is thus; sometimes it is not thus. The weights on the scale are adjusted as appropriate;

the length of the cloth under the ruler is cut according to my will. As for bringing peace to the nation and happiness to the people, conforming to custom and harmonizing with the times—[it is all within this].

The light unifies the four seas into a single family and brings together the hundred rivers into a single flavor; yet this is still merely a peripheral matter concerning the universal invitation of all directions.
Consider, for instance, the vast breadth of the sea-gate shore and the towering height of Mount Fuyü: waves surge a thousand fathoms high, and clouds stretch across ten thousand layers.
Furthermore, where else would one look for another’s flaw? Striking his knee, he said: "Were it not for Ren Gongzi, all talk of fishing rods would be in vain.
He then cited an instance: One day, while Master Xuedou was seated with Minister Li, a scholar and a Daoist entered.
The Minister asked, "Among the three teachings, which is the most honored? Xuedou rose and turned his body sideways.
Xuedou stood there. Dadian said, "Having a mouth, why do you not speak? Xuedou said, "In the presence of a Master, it is difficult to speak. The Master [Zhaozhou] took up the case, saying:

"Great as Xuedou was, he was reduced to standing with his body turned aside by a single question from Dadian. Had there been no subsequent words, he would have been caught off guard and 'the city of Caizhou' would have been broken."
Ascending the hall: Night is dark, day is bright; heaven is level, earth is level. Rain every three days, sun every five days.
Great Master Bodhidharma did not abide by his own lot and was beaten until his front teeth fell out. Master Guizong of Mount Lu groundlessly rubbed out a pair of eyes.
(He picks up the staff and strikes once. Those in the same pit have no different soil.
Ascending the hall, he said: "A phrase that can be spoken on the crossroads of the city is of no use in a village of three households.
A phrase that can be spoken in a village of three households is of no use on the crossroads of the city.
Nevertheless, whether at the crossroads or in the village, if you have money you ride a horse; if you have no money, you drive an ox."
The Buddha ascends the hall for his final nirvana. Before Mount Zhengjue, beneath the twin śāla trees, he plays with the false as if it were real, and plays with the real as if it were false.
He bellows in the wind like Dai Song’s ox; he neighs while gazing at his reflection like Han Gan’s horse.
Do you all see the Old Śākyamuni? Holding up his whisk, he says: "He comes! He comes!"
Ascending the hall, he called to the assembly and pointed to his nose with his hand, saying: "Throughout my life, this monk has been obstructed by this very thing.
Is there anyone here who can apply a lethal blow and pluck it away for me? If you can pluck it away, I grant you all a place of peace and ease throughout the twelve hours of the day.
If you cannot pluck it away, when incense reaches the nose, it is also called 'stealing.'"
Ascending the hall, he said: "Today is the first day of the seventh month; tomorrow is the second day of the seventh month. One day is one day—how many here know how to feel shame?
(Looking at the assembly) Is there anyone? Is there anyone? Then, shaking his hand, he said: "It is not so. It is not so."
Ascending the hall to thank the former and new stewards as well as the supervisors and collectors: within stillness there is movement; within movement there is stillness.
Yet, amidst this movement and stillness, there is no discrimination, nor is even a hair’s breadth of the marks of movement or stillness perceived.
Since the marks of movement and stillness cannot be apprehended, then every movement and stillness, every exit and entry, every release and gathering, every advance...
A single retreat—there is nothing that is not the playful exercise of spiritual powers and luminosity within the realm of liberation.
Since this is so, it is like speaking in silence and being silent while speaking; the lion’s roar and the jackal’s cry, the jackal’s cry and the lion’s roar—are they ultimately distinct or not?
After a long pause: “Do you understand? The water beneath Mount Dongting; the clouds atop the peaks of Mount Nanyue.”
Ascending the hall on the Double Ninth: "Double Yang, the ninth day of the ninth month—everyone knows this well. Having drunk the chrysanthemum tea, most have their brows furrowed.
Only Tao Jingjie alone wears a joyful countenance; he can say: 'Picking chrysanthemums beneath the eastern hedge, I leisurely behold the Southern Mountains.
Nevertheless, his worldly air has not been removed."
Ascending the hall on the occasion of the Shuìqìng Festival, he raised [the following] case: Dōngshān said, "If one discusses this matter, it is like the twenty-four provinces of a nation.
If the news from even a single province does not reach [the capital], then one is failing to serve the sovereign.

According to what Jiāoshān observes today, it may be called a season of Great Peace; it is not merely that the twenty-four provinces are so, but rather that it extends to every speck of dust and hair.
Throughout the ocean of lands, there is no message that does not reach its destination. Once the message has been conveyed, one serves the sovereign with total loyalty.
"The wind follows the tiger; the clouds follow the dragon.
[He] ascended the hall and raised this case: A monk asked an ancient worthy, "After the birth of the first yang, the days grow by one thread. I wonder, does the Buddha-dharma also grow?"
"How much? De-yun replied, "One thread longer. Later, another ancient worthy said, "One thread longer.
The Master said, "What was said before and what was said after are as far apart as heaven and earth.
If you can distinguish them clearly, you will have a point of entry into the Buddha-dharma. People nowadays mostly swallow it whole, as the saying goes:"
Vague about Buddha-nature; muddled about True Suchness. It is like using fish eyes to confuse one with bright pearls.

[The Master] ascends the hall and says: "The Buddha Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū sat upon the site of enlightenment for ten kalpas, yet the Buddha-dharma did not manifest before him, and he could not attain the Way of Buddhahood.
Since he sat upon the site of enlightenment for ten kalpas, why was the Buddha-dharma not manifest before him? Why could he not attain it?
He attained the Way of the Buddha. From of old, Jiaoshan has harbored doubts regarding this fellow.
Recorded by the attendants Rūha and Mialun et al., from the *Recorded Sayings* of the Chan Master at Zisheng Chan Temple on Mount Xuedou in Qingyuan Prefecture.
In the Buddha Hall, Kāśyapa raised his joined palms and Ānanda pressed his palms together; the Yellow-Faced Gautama was utterly without skill.
At once, the New Milk Peak was fully revealed, and he then burned aloeswood incense as an offering. Let people say it is a punishment or let them say it is a reward.
He sat upon the square mat; De-yun did not descend from the summit of Mount Miaofeng, and Shancai spent seven days searching for him without success.
"Hūṃ! Hūṃ! You lot, what on earth are you waiting for here with those blinking eyes?
Why don't you go off already? Don't hinder me as I move about from east to west! Having said this, he struck the meditation seat and rose.

He pointed to the Dharma seat and said: "This is the 'One Stroke' atop the crowns of a thousand sages. From antiquity until now, few have ever trodden upon it, and rare indeed are those who have raised it up.
Today, as I walk along, I shall not hesitate to swing my arm across it."

Having ascended the seat and finished the prayers for the Emperor (the questions and answers are not recorded), he then said: "The path of the patch-robed monk lies neither in the east nor in the west;
meeting conditions, one takes them as the source, responding to circumstances as they arise. Yesterday was the Elder of Jiaoshan; today is the Master of Xuedou.
Casting aside the ten-thousand-mile expanse of misty waves at Haimen, we come to behold the wind and moon over the entire valley at Miaogao Terrace. Both sound and form..."

All is obliterated; right and wrong have vanished into the distance. For the great, they are great; for the small, they are small. Cease attempting to measure and evaluate them through the lens of Buddha-dharma.
The mountains are green again, and the waters are lush again. Do not interpret this as a description of external objects. Since you do not interpret it as such, how then will you understand it?
Even if there were painters of the human world with the skill of hand and brush, it would be difficult to capture it within a painting.
Again, it is cited: A monk asked Touzi, "What is the Ten-Body Tamer? Touzi descended from his meditation seat and stood there.
The Master said, "The assembly, Touzi’s doing so is not without merit; nevertheless, he still fails to avoid troubling his venerable guest.
Had I been there at that time, I would have simply performed a deep bow right before him, causing this old fellow to hide away."
The body has no path.

That evening, there was a small *sīmān* (informal discourse). "Without giving rise to a single thought—before the time of Vidyottama, even when Maitreya descends to be born—he cuts off all manifold distinctions.
Whether in Jambudvīpa to the south or Uttarakuru to the north—if you can understand it thus, then you shall not depart from the site of enlightenment (*bodhimaṇḍa*)."

Ascending the summit of Mount Miaofeng, one immediately encounters a profusion of water and clouds, where ordinary beings and sages mingle. There, self and other are forgotten and host and guest find harmony in the Way.
When seated, they sit together; when walking, they walk together. Returning, they return hand-in-hand; arriving, everyone arrives together.
It is indeed arrival—but as for what occurs therein, how can it be described? A thousand-fathom snow falls as rain, and the *yange* tree lies prostrate.
"Ten thousand pine trees. He raised the case again: "Master Bodhidharma said: 'I have come to this land to transmit the Dharma and save deluded beings.
One flower opens into five petals; the gate is naturally formed. The Master said: 'If the Patriarch spoke thus, he deserves thirty blows of the staff.
But tell me, why is it so? Because winter is exercising the ordinances of spring."
I thank the two classes of assembly for ascending the hall. It is now the first day of the first month, yet five days have already passed. Worldly affairs are as tangled as hemp;
time flies as swiftly as a split arrow. Therefore it is said: "When this day has passed, one's life is likewise diminished; like a fish in scant water."
What joy is there in this? Look at the Milk-Peak; what could be more delightful than that? To the east are the administrators, and to the west are the heads of the community.
This mountain monk has won the freedom to lean against the railing, gazing up all day as the clouds drift by.
A-ha! People often mistake this for a song of mountain dwelling.
Ascending the hall, he said: "A clear spring day; yellow orioles sing. Mountain flowers are like brocade; marsh grasses are like carpets. How pitiable and how laughable!
Officer Wang, the patrolman from Gongtang Village, goes everywhere on his rounds, yet he himself does not realize that he has lost a pair of eyes.
After a long silence, he said: "The colorful rush belongs to the petty householder."
Husheng Xiaojingci arrived; he ascended the hall and said: "It is related that Zen Master Furong visited Grand Master Shixing.
When the Grand Master ascended the hall, he took his staff in his right hand, placed it on his left side, and said: 'If it were not for my elder brother, Master Furong...'"
He spoke at length regarding this great difficulty and then descended from his seat. Later, Chan Master Nanyuan of Huanglong said: "If one cannot employ the true nature, then simply stop;
yet you instead use the Buddha-dharma to accommodate human sentiments, thereby causing it to become a laughingstock for all time."
The Master said: "The Great Master Shixing was selling stolen goods on the crossroads and yet still claimed no one knew of it.
Old Huanglong could not bear to see this and skillfully tried to conceal it for him. Little did he know that the more one tries to hide it, the more it is revealed.
Nevertheless, while it is easy to see the Great Master Shixing, it is somewhat difficult to see Huanglong. Why? Because..."
Tatou’s forehead was as flat as a fan. He ascended the hall and said:
“When Lingyun saw the peach blossoms, he immediately declared, ‘I no longer have any doubt. Xuansha also said, ‘He has not yet reached the ultimate.
Later, Wuzu also said, ‘Do not speak of not having reached the ultimate; you must practice for another thirty years before you will attain it. I, this mountain monk, have once... [tried it].”
When I heard it said that there were three snakes and nine mice on a single mu of land, at first I did not believe it;
looking at this today, I find the former words to be true.
On the occasion of the Dragon Boat Festival, he ascended the hall and raised the koan of Mañjuśrī instructing Sudhana to gather medicinal herbs. The Master said:
"According to Sudhana, everything he gathered was nothing but medicine; yet, alas, he mistakenly took licorice for yellow bitter.
Mañjuśrī knew only that it could both kill and give life, but he did not know its origin. Setting Mañjuśrī aside for a moment..."
Holding up his staff, he said, "Everyone, tell me: from where did this come? Ultimately, is it bitter gall (*harītakī*) or licorice (*madhuka*)?
He struck the ground once and said, "There is plenty in South of the River; there is none at all in North of the River."

Ascending the hall for a discourse on a particular matter: this very case is already manifest and complete. Among the assembly, there are many who have attained understanding, yet not a few who have misunderstood it.
Consequently, gold and brass cannot be distinguished, and jade and stone are difficult to tell apart.
Here at Lurong, I intend to distinguish them clearly: Layman Zhang and Layman Li—one has long arms, the other has large eyes. Both...
"It is like the single school of Bodhidharma today—teaching what kind of person to carry its burden? He let out a long sigh and descended from his seat.
On the anniversary of Master Po’an’s passing, he offered incense and said: "This old bald-head has no face; he lacks even a trace of compassion, yet possesses tenfold malice.
When he is pleased, one cannot draw near him; when he is angry, one especially cannot touch him. In the past, I was forbidden by him."
It is a torment! It has driven this stubborn snake to sprout feet, so that until this very day, as I burn a single stick of incense and offer three prostrations in vain, I can neither laugh nor cry.
How shall this grievance and this resentment be avenged? Oṃ bulin oṃ chilin.
Ascending the hall, the Master said: "Since I entered this monastery, half a year has passed. I have never yet spoken to you all regarding the matter of our own fundamental nature.
Today, moreover, it coincides with the anniversary of the passing of the Patriarch Mingjue;
we have gone to the stupa for the communal recitation of sutras, so there was no leisure to speak. Nevertheless, look: are the eyebrows of Lufeng still there?"
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "I do not understand the Buddha-dharma, nor do I understand the worldly dharma. In these ninety days of a summer retreat, blind donkeys follow the great crowd.
But in the end, what have they actually accomplished? He then said: "I do not know."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Two arise because of one; yet do not cling even to that one. At noon in Silla, they strike the watch of three.

Turning back your head, look southward at the Northern Dipper. How pitiable and how laughable! These yellow-faced Chan practitioners travel everywhere on foot, doing nothing but sniffing their nostrils from the east to the west.
On the very tip of their own noses, there is a speck of dung—ten or five pairs of them!"
"Why do you not perceive the stench?
[The Master] ascended the hall and said: "I recall that in the past, Chan Master Chang of Damei asked Master Ma, 'What is the Buddha?
Master Ma replied, 'This very mind is the Buddha. He then took root right here; he could no longer move or turn. After he settled there..."

Someone asked, "What is the meaning of [the Master’s] coming from the West? Mei said, "There is no meaning in coming from the West. After a long silence, he said, "As expected. He ascended the hall and said:
"A person of genuine character who travels on pilgrimage must possess the eye of pilgrimage. Of the thousands and tens of thousands, most are merely carrying empty wooden boards.
Setting aside for a moment the matter of carrying these boards, what is the eye of pilgrimage? In the morning look to the southeast; in the evening observe..."
Northwest. Ascending the hall: The wind whistles, the rain whistles; travelers have their bows and arrows each at their waists.

The old bearded barbarian from Shaolin, with his missing teeth, stubbornly did not know there was anything else—yet he turned toward the wall for nine years at Shao-lin. But even so, it was not on the wall. You all—
"Each and every one of you gentlemen—why not turn your hands over and feel about?

[The Master] thanked the Head Seat and ascended the hall. He cited the public case of the lay practitioner Gan-zhi entering Nanquan’s hall for a vegetarian feast, where he requested the Head Seat to give away his wealth.
The Master said: "He spoke thus at the beginning; why did he not offer a monetary gift? He spoke thus at the end as well."
The Way. For what reason did he immediately bestow his alms? Today, by way of walking with his arms swinging, he has added this footnote: "The straight within the curved;

the curved within the straight. There is increase and decrease; there are countless points. He casually places it before a dark window, leaving people to gaze at it in silence, never weary of the view.
Ascending the hall on the Double Ninth, he took up his staff, placed it across the desk, and said: "If you understand it thus, there is an intercalary month once every three years;
if you do not understand, it is simply the Double Ninth. He struck the desk once and said: "This only wins the laughter of those who understand, breaking one's heart."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The sutras have masters of the sutras; the treatises have masters of the treatises. At this place on Milk Peak, what could I possibly say?
Today, I shall let down a single thread of the path and follow the custom of dividing it into sections and paragraphs.
With his right hand, he took up his staff, struck the ground once, and placed it to his left. He asked, "What chapter or verse is this? Then he said, "The Section on Circulation."
Ascending the hall, he raised [the following] case: "Recently, Master Ruiyan addressed the assembly, citing an ancient precedent:

'When the autumn river is clear and shallow, the white dew mingles with the misty isles. How excellent is Avalokiteśvara! His entire body enters the wild weeds. When the ancient worthy spoke thus, it was as if saying:
'Jade is naturally flawless, yet it possesses flaws. Ruiyan, however, does not agree. When the autumn river is clear and shallow, the white dew mingles with the mist..."
Island. For ten years he could not return; he forgot the path by which he came. The Master said: "Ruigan speaking thus may indeed be called flawless.
Yet today I shall provide another path for him, so that all quarters may examine and critique it:
When the autumn river is clear and shallow, white dew mingles with the misty island. Leaning on my staff amidst the silence, I gaze until I am lost, for no one comes. He struck the meditation seat.
Descend from your seat. Ascend the hall. Three fingers above and below; seven horses for both sides. As if existing, as if non-existent; half-real, half-false.
When Nanyue Huairang was questioned about this, he could not provide an explanation for five years. Aha-ha! He laughed the old man of East Village down.

Elder Sister, when ascending the hall: to speak is slander; silence is deception. To intend is already to deviate; to move is already to lose it. Even those with clear eyes find it difficult to draw near.

Severing worldly passions and forgetting all artifice: On the occasion of the Festival of the Establishment of Heaven, the Great Master Mazu of Jiangxi and National Teacher Huairang of Nanyue ascended the hall. "Upon this Milk Peak there is a lute; it is not made of *jiao* wood, nor is it of ordinary timber."
For many years it has hung upon the wall, never easily played. Today, fortunately, we encounter the auspicious occasion of the new Emperor’s sacred birthday;
as this favorable day has arrived, it must not be missed. I shall try playing one piece to celebrate his ten-thousand-year reign.
He then assumes the posture for playing the lute and says: *Ding-dang, ding-dang.* After a long while, he asks: "Do you understand?"
I vow to offer this song in perpetual service to the Sage and Enlightened Ruler.
Ascending the Hall to thank the former and current administrators: Within the gate of worldly convention (*saṃvṛti*), there is new and old, coming and going, advancing and retreating.
However, regarding the ultimate Dharma (*paramārtha*), there is neither high nor low, neither "that" nor "this," and neither factionalism nor partiality. Although...
"Indeed so. But which of these few things is the Buddha-dharma? Which of these few things is worldly convention?
Try, for the sake of Lufeng, to pull out even a single strand of hair and show it to me. After a long silence, he said, "Why do you act so foolishly?"
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The old fellow Deshan spent his entire life wielding a single white staff; he would strike even if a Buddha came, and he would strike even if an Ancestor came.
Yet he claimed that he had never struck a single person who was truly liberated. He even shouted at people as they went down the eastern corridor."

Xihang also shouted "He! down from above. Even if you could shout so that Xinghua were sent up to the thirty-third heaven and then dashed back down until he had not a breath of life left, and waited for Xinghua to slowly regain his composure, I would say to you: "It is not yet."
Do you all know where these two great elders stand? Heaven is high in the southeast; the earth slopes toward the northwest.
On the day of the winter solstice, he ascends the hall: "One winter, two winters. With hands folded across the chest, the pearl drills through the nine bends—straightness is right there within them.
Ascending the hall: On the first full moon of the first month, the lanterns reach across the Milky Way. A thousand people and ten thousand people gather their heads together to look at them.
There is no lack of looking, but first, each must take care of his own eyes. Lurong did not grant him any concession; in the end, he struck him down.
Since he has been struck down, with what will you distinguish the black from the white? After a long silence, he said: "Mañjuśrī."
Touzi Bai and Puxian Touhei. [Touzi] ascends the hall and says:
He cites a monk asking Master Mazu, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
Master Mazu said, "Come closer, and I will tell you. When the monk stepped forward, Master Mazu gave him a slap. The monk said, "Why did you strike me?"
Master Ma said, "Six ears do not share a secret. Later, Chan Master Nanyuan of Huanglong said, "The ancients still said that six ears do not share a secret;
nowadays, the various quarters are engaged in a vast clamor of discussion—this is a calamity. The Master called to the assembly, saying:
"Trusting the books entirely is not as good as having no books at all.
He ascended the hall and said, "Within the lands of the ten directions, there is only the Single Vehicle Dharma. Do you all believe this?
If you can believe it thoroughly, I will drag the country of Campā and the country of Silla to fight over the forehead. If you cannot believe it, [you must go] to the head of Caishi Ferry."
The Boat.
Picking Tea and Ascending the Hall. When masters meet, there is something upon which they rely. In a place utterly devoid of people, they gather their heads together to converse.
Jizi, for no reason, shook the tea tree.
Ascending the hall for the opening of the summer retreat, he held up his staff and, looking toward the assembly, said: "The summer retreat is completed; the holy life is established;
what was to be done has been accomplished. Yet Venerable Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja has, without cause, stirred thoughts here.
I shall cast him away to the two Iron Ring Mountains. He struck the ground once with the staff and said: "Contemplate closely the Dharma of the Dharma King; such is the Dharma of the Dharma King."

Ascending the hall on the Double Fifth Festival, a monk asked: "When Mañjuśrī ordered Sudhana to gather medicinal herbs, and Sudhana said, 'Bring back whatever you consider to be medicine,' what was the meaning?
The Master said, "The intent lies at the tip of the hook. The monk pressed further: "Sudhana then said, 'There is nothing in the entire universe that is not medicine.
What about that? The Master said, "Do not mistake aconite for *chuanniao*. The monk continued: "And what about Mañjuśrī?"
[The Master] said, "This medicine has been brought here; where does its meaning lie? The Master said, "That is another fine squeeze.

The monk advanced and said, "When Sudhana picked up a blade of grass from the ground and offered it to Mañjuśrī, Mañjuśrī said, 'This medicine can kill a person, and it can also bring a person to life.
I do not know what the meaning of this was. The Master said, "They were deceiving one another. The monk bowed.
The Master raised his staff and said: "Today is the fifth day of the fifth month, the Dragon Boat Festival. At Lufeng, I have obtained a prescription for medicine.
It was not left behind by Jīvaka, nor was it transmitted by Bian Que. Although it is not worth a single coin, it nevertheless treats every ailment.
This includes what are called the Buddha-illness, the Patriarch-illness, the Zen-illness, the mind-illness, and all manner of maladies. Whoever takes this..."

[Those who were ill] all attained complete recovery. The "Milk Peak" (the breast) did not dare to be stingy; today, beating the drum and ascending the hall, it is bestowed universally upon the great assembly.
If one who is ill comes, it is entrusted to the left hand; if one who is not ill comes, it is entrusted to the right hand. But tell me, why is it so?
It is neither existent nor non-existent, neither non-existent nor not non-existent. [He] then struck [the meditation seat] once and said: "Zhaozhou."
A gourd hangs on the eastern wall.

[The Master] ascends the hall: "With a straight hook one catches whales and turtles; with a curved hook one catches fish and tortoises. I, Ruyong, have a rough understanding of what is good and what is bad, and I do not dare to suppress you all. He then descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, he said: "In recent years, the Hu tribes have been extinguished from our sight; the monastic groves rejoice in seeing times of peace.

Who can entrust them with the news of this peace? Only Zhang Gong and Old Li know it. But as for what they know—how so? In the eastern province the rice is ripe; in the western province the rice is cheap."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The myriad trees are startled by the frosty wind; the thousand forests are clothed in autumn colors. How laughable is this man Hanshan—nowhere can he be found!
[He] picks up his staff and says: 'So it turns out he is right here! Look, look! He strikes the floor once and says:
'And now he has gone back inside the pillar.'"

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "The autumn wind blows steadily; the autumn colors linger on. Upon the ridge, white clouds drift by in sheets; beside the fence, yellow chrysanthemums stand in clusters of three or five.
How many in this world climb the heights? They merely focus on ascending step by step, yet they often fail to notice that beneath their own feet they have already slipped past.
For me to speak thus, O Lurong, is like painting a tiger and ending up with a wildcat."

Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Today at Lurong, the furnace is opened. We do not know how to pick up ashes or stir the embers; everyone simply wraps themselves in their patched robes and sits together in a circle.
We seek nothing from the various sages, nor do we prize our own spiritual brilliance. From outside these gates, there is the weary toil of the worldly path, the restless turmoil of the red dust.
Summer ends and autumn begins; autumn ends and winter begins; winter ends and spring begins. After a long silence, he said: "Reflect upon this."
He also admired the Western Qin.
Entering the hall, he raised [the following] case: Master Baiyun Dan addressed Wuzu, saying, "There is one matter; do you, elder brother, know it?"
The Patriarch said, "I do not know what matters there are. Duan said, "Recently several Chan practitioners came from Mount Lu.
They claimed to have attained a state of awakening; they could explain it, compose verses on it, and provide critical commentaries on it—but it was simply not yet sufficient.
When the Fifth Patriarch heard this, for seven days and seven nights he could not digest his food. The Master said:
Master Baiyun exhausted his own mind and laughed the mouths of others to pieces.
Here at Lufeng, there is also one matter that I cannot help but tell you all. Recently, several Zen practitioners have come from various quarters;
they have no place of awakening when questioned, and they are unable to speak or compose verses when asked to do so. [The master] struck them.
This judgment cannot be critiqued. Nevertheless, Lufeng nevertheless grants that he is a person who has brought everything to completion and resolution.
When you all hear this, there is no need to harbor doubts. Why? Because [he is] South Tiantai and North Wutai.
Ascending the hall, he said: "The single phrase prior to sound leaves nothing behind and establishes nothing; it cuts off the tongue.
How can one express it? Yesterday someone came from Tiantai and went on to Jingshan."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said: "Linji was misled by Muzhou; Xuefeng suffered the lethal blow of Yantou.

They harbored this grievance until their final days, an indignation that shall remain undecaying for ten thousand generations. Therefore, students should reflect deeply upon the sound of the 'ding-ding' wood-cutting axe.
Shining light upon the past and illuminating the present, you should seek out true friends with diligence."
Ascending the hall, he called to the assembly, saying: "Zen! Zen! At the summit of Mount Sumeru, before a thousand-fathom cliff, how can there be an ancient pine tree?
It is strange and wondrous; it is crooked and twisted; it is gnarled and contorted. If you all understand it in this way, you will be as far from it as ever."
The Head Seat, the Librarian, and the Chief Administrator take up the whisk; for the midday meal, he ascends the hall.
An ancient said, "Before the wheel of Dharma turns, the wheel of food turns first. Here at Lurong, both wheels turn together.
Since both wheels turn, this assembly before me hears the Dharma never heard before and receives food such as has never been obtained. The power of this food extends to the seventh...
Only after the sun has risen does it finally vanish. Once this food has been digested, the method is also forgotten.
This does not hinder them from gathering in groups of three or two by the water’s edge or beneath the trees, calling out to one another as they stroll together.

Ascending the hall, he raised an example: Once, Danxia visited an ancient temple. After staying overnight, when the morning congee was ready, the attendant filled one bowl and offered it to the temple, then filled another bowl for himself to eat, paying no attention whatsoever to Danxia. Danxia then filled his own bowl and ate.
The other said, "At the fifth watch, rising before dawn, there are still travelers on the road at night. Xiang then asked the temple abbot, "Why do you not instruct this traveler?
He is so impolite! The abbot replied, "One must not defile the clean ground with the presence of people's sons and daughters.
Xiang said, "I am wary of not questioning the faults of this old fellow. The Master said, "Though the traveler is good at receiving those of high standing..."
"Guests, how regrettable that my resources are so meager! Danxia does not know how to be a guest; I cannot help but trouble you, my host.

At that time, had he simply filled his own bowl with congee and eaten it, then taken up his staff and departed, he would have spared this ancient temple from being stained—yet here, in the midst of avoiding defilement, he has instead created one.
How, then, can this be avoided? After a long silence, he descended from the seat and went around the hall to drink tea with the assembly.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "In front is a precipice ten thousand fathoms deep; behind is a thicket of brambles;
on both sides are blazing fires, with a mass of flames in the center. How can one turn back? The old fellow Zhaozhou made a cotton robe while in Qingzhou that weighed seven catties."
On the first day of the New Year, he ascended the hall because of the snow: "This morning, the first day of the first month, is nothing but an ordinary day.
Yet, within it lies a point of extraordinary distinction: the entire world is spread with silver. Since the world of silver has already appeared, where is Samantabhadra?
Raising his staff, he said, "Look! Look! Seeing that the assembly would not turn their attention toward him, he could not help but mount his six-tusked fragrant elephant and enter.
I go to Mount Wutai to offer New Year’s greetings to my elder brother Mañjuśrī.

*He strikes the sounding block once.* Ascending the hall for the dispersal of the assembly on the occasion of the National Foundation Day: The Way of the King is level and plain; his longevity is continuous and far-reaching.
Fishermen’s songs and woodcutters’ chants together rejoice in the era of Yao. No-action, indeed; no partiality, indeed. Heaven and Earth are unified within these ancient mountains and rivers.
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and called to the assembly, saying: "Those who have not yet attained, upon seeing this staff, call it a 'staff.
But when one who has attained speaks of it, what do they call it? If you can say, [he] strikes once and says: 'Right now, you enter the earth.
If you cannot say, [he] leans on the staff and says: 'Wait until the roots sprout.'"
Xie Tiantongyan ascends the high seat for the inaugural lecture: "Ten thousand distinctions and a thousand differences—when engaged in affairs, they are like one family.
When affairs are like one family, there are ten thousand distinctions and a thousand differences. Before Mount Taibai, the water-mill turns day and night without ceasing;
within Lufeng Temple, the assembly retires from meditation to drink tea."
The Head Official (shoushou) held the whisk, and the Abbot (duwei) ascended the hall for the midday meal. Though he lacked any sense of awe, he spoke great empty words;
though free from any longing, he discerned the supreme offering. Nevertheless, one must be a person of great shamelessness to be able to satiate oneself with the flavor of the Dharma.
As for all other inferior weeds, they cannot avoid the fate of encountering it yet not encountering it. For now, let us set aside those who do not encounter it.
Let us not discuss that further. But consider this: does one who has eaten their fill have any way to repay that kindness? He then lets out two sounds of eructation and descends from his seat.
On the occasion of the Longevity Festival, he ascends the hall and says: "The *Prajñāpāramitā* is the mother of Bodhisattvas; it contains and receives all dharmas. Yet, regarding all dharmas..."

Yet one is free from the marks of conceptual discrimination. Once discrimination is abandoned, all phenomena are suchness (tathatā). Ten thousand branches of the Shu River flow toward the vast blue sea;
a thousand fathoms of the Min Ridge pierce the great void.
Ascending the hall. The drum was struck and he ascended the hall; the assembly gathered like clouds. There is something to deliberate upon regarding the Buddha-dharma: today is as hot as yesterday.

Ascending the hall at the conclusion of the retreat period, one must realize the proof within the fixed time. Tying up a blind donkey. At the end of the summer retreat, one speaks of one’s own realization; do not speak like a ghost.
Let you have a seat for now. Once seated, there is another way of life. If you go to other places, do not say that you spent the summer retreat here.
Why? Xuedou personally dwelt to the east of Bao’ai.

After the formal bows, [the Master] ascends the seat in the Rear Hall and says: "In the assembly of Zhaozhou, there were two monks who pushed each other aside, refusing to accept the position of the First Seat.
The administrative official informed Zhaozhou of this. Zhaozhou said, 'Let them both take the Second Seat. The official asked:"
Zhaozhou said, "Who shall I instruct to take the seat of honor? The attendant replied, "Incense has been prepared. Zhaozhou said, "The fragrance of precepts;
the fragrance of meditative concentration. The Master remarked, "Zhaozhou the old fellow is indeed so, yet he moves at the slightest touch and turns at the slightest pressure."
But alas, hands and feet are all revealed at once. Here at Ruyong Peak, there is no need for such mutual pushing.
If you wish to recognize the first seat, it is the second seat; if you wish to recognize the second seat, it is the first seat. After a long silence, he said:
Before the Peak of Shaoshi, one who was lost encountered Bodhidharma.

He ascended the hall and said: "The autumn deepens, increasing the crisp air; the night grows cold, adding the need for a double-layered quilt. Grass insects chirp at the base of the walls; yellow leaves drift across the courtyard.
This mountain monk tosses and turns, unable to sleep for joy. A-he-he! To stretch out one's legs is the original state."

While [the assembly] was huddled with their legs tucked in, Master Shiyuan arrived. He ascended the hall and, holding up his staff, said: "For a long time I have kept this essential matter silent, not seeking to speak of it hastily.

Now that I have encountered those who recognize it, jade and stone can no longer be hidden from one another. Since they cannot be hidden, he raised his staff and said: "For now, let us call this thing..."
"What is it? Is it jade, or is it stone? [The Master] struck his staff and said, "Distinguish them" (the expression of thanks is not recorded). He further raised the case:
Ānanda asked Kāśyapa, "Aside from the transmission of the golden robe, what else did the World-Honored One transmit?

The Master said, "Face to face, looking at one another; eye to eye, staring intently. Aside from the robe, what evidence is there for a separate transmission? Knock over the banner-pole in front of the gate!"
[The Master] ascended the hall on the Mid-Autumn Festival for the benefit of Brother Xie Beijing and others.
"The flaming torch preaches the Dharma for the Buddhas of the three periods; the Buddhas of the three periods stand upon the ground and listen.
Listening is at the place of speaking; speaking is at the place of listening. When both speaking and listening are forgotten, how can one analyze it?"
The *Lü* entered the Canon and the Chan returned to the Sea; it was only this "Horse Winnowing Basket" that possessed a wealth of playful gestures.
Whenever one encounters the time for viewing the moon on the Mid-Autumn Festival, reflecting upon it truly makes one cherish it. Why? Have you not heard it said: "The winnowing basket has lips"?
The rice will not leap out.
[The Master] enters the hall. He raises the case: A monk asked Changsha, "How can one turn the mountains, rivers, and the great earth back into oneself?
Changsha said, "How can one turn oneself back into the mountains, rivers, and the great earth? Later, Dahui said, "Turn the mountains..."
It is easy to turn the rivers, the great earth, and all things back into oneself; it is difficult to turn oneself back into the rivers, the great earth, and all things.
If there is anyone who can utter a phrase that is neither difficult nor easy, come to Mount Jing’s hands and ask for a blow from my staff. The Master called to the assembly, saying:
For the family of patch-robed monks, even one's own self is not seen to exist; from where could the mountains, rivers, and the great earth have come? Furthermore, what more could be turned over?
Old fellow Dahui, for no reason, followed up by speaking of the difficult and the easy. He struck the meditation seat and said:
"To gain the mouth is to lose the nose."
