Ascending the hall, he said: "Level and smooth as a mirror; curved and bent like a hook. No one can gather it up;
it is cast away upon a heap of dung. Can you all gather it up? After a long silence, he said: "The sprout has grown."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Going, going—yet truly not going; on the road, act with goodness. Coming, coming—yet truly not coming; on the path, do not stumble or fall.
When the ancients spoke thus, they were merely treading upon the ground for fear of pain. At Lurong, it is otherwise: when one wishes to go, one goes;
when one wishes to come, one comes. What need is there to "act with goodness"? And where is there any danger of stumbling? It is simply that yesterday...
As the sun passed over the New Ridge, the floodwaters surged and swept away three sections of the stone bridge; yet the mountain monk crossed them all with effortless ease.
This morning, as the drum was beaten and the hall ascended, you lot came here intending to seek the Buddha-dharma.
After a long silence, he said: "For now, proceed slowly."
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and showed it to the assembly, saying, "Maitreya is truly Maitreya; he manifests himself in thousands of billions of bodies.
From time to time he reveals himself to those who seek him. He leaned on the staff and, springing forward, said, "Do you all recognize him?
Most people would likely mistake this for a transmission of the Venerable Subhūti. Thereupon, he descended from the seat.

Ascending the hall on the Winter Solstice: "The season arrives as the clouds record the day; the first yang is born on this very day. Once the first yang is born, the myriad phenomena come forth to life.
Once the myriad phenomena have come forth, there is nothing that does not come forth. Raising his staff, he said, "Tell me, how many things has this staff brought to life?
After a long silence, he said, "It is more than seven feet long," and struck it once.
The Head Seat Xie holds the whisk; the Administrative Head delivers the lecture for the winter retreat. The flavorless is the true flavor; the true flavor is truly flavorless.
If one knows the true flavor, one speaks no more of the true flavor. I have heard it said that once full, one forgets a hundred hungers;
today, this mountain monk’s body sets forth at once.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Of the three hundred and sixty days of the year, look, they are nearly exhausted. As it is said:
'On the night when the year draws to its close, there are those who have not yet returned from the four seas. Yet those who have not yet returned must surely go back.
And as for those who have already returned, they must not remain fixed in their hometowns. Why? Because sitting too long leads to weariness."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the following case: A monk asked Yunmen, "What is the 'Single Tune of Yunmen'? Yunmen said, "The twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month. The Master said:
"The Single Tune of Yunmen has never had a musical score from the beginning. Its resonance transcends the five notes; its melody is sublime for a thousand ages.
Among these, who can understand the wondrous intent? How many times have people tried to cast Ziqi in gold?"
Ascending the hall on the occasion of the National Foundation Day: "The Way of sovereign and subject is in harmony; this is precisely the matter of the Dharma-body (dharmakāya).
But what is the matter beyond the Dharma-body? Atop Mount Zhurong stands the ten-thousand-year-old pine; its roots coil and its trunk soars, transcending the azure heavens."
When the old friend arrived at the hall (Shanyan’s “Womb-Bird”), he held up his staff and showed it to the assembly, saying: "I have a phrase that is neither sweet nor bitter.
Now that I have met one who understands, how shall I express it? He struck once, saying: "Last night I lit a 'willow-stag';
now it has turned into a 'tail-tiger'. He struck again.
The Buddha ascends the hall for his final nirvana. On Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa, the creeping vines of entanglement spread their tendrils and branches throughout the world.
After Māra, filled with shame, has toppled them, there is a path from east to west for people to walk upon. Nevertheless, you must still look carefully where your feet tread.
Record of the Sayings at Guangli Chan Temple on Mount Ayuwang in Qingyuan Prefecture, compiled by the attendants Wenyi, Liaoxin, and others.
Introduction to the Three Gates: This great gate of liberation is that through which we enter and exit together with all people every day, playing therein.
In the meantime, for every step you take, I, this mountain monk, also take one step; for every two steps you take, I, this mountain monk, also take two steps.
While one or two steps are easy to compare, three or five steps are more difficult. You must look for yourself at the top of your feet and the soles of your feet.
Pointing to the Dharma seat, he said: "The Great Assembly, Mount Sumeru Lamp King never fails to preach the Great Prajñāpāramitā for all people.
Do you hear it? If you have not yet realized this, Mount Maofeng shall proceed from the 'Introductory Chapter' once more."
Having ascended the seat and finished the prayers for the Emperor (the questions and answers are not recorded), he said: "Before forms and names had manifested, the jade was inherently flawless.
Once its patterns and brilliance were revealed, the object returned to having a master. Add a little, and Zhang San breaks out in malice;
subtract a little, and Li Si gives rise to anger. Without adding or subtracting—Yunmen’s fan leaps up into the sky and strikes the nostrils of Śakra, the Lord of the East."
"A sea carp is struck with a blow; the rain pours down like an overturned basin. At such a time, how do you speak of it? After a long silence, he said:
"The Southern Mountain remains as ever level with the clouds. He then raised the kōan of King Aśoka asking the Venerable Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja, "Have you personally seen the Buddha?
He commented: "King Aśoka asked this quite casually, yet it turned out to be a growth outside the joints."
[The Buddha] held up a branch. Piṇḍola faced him directly and held it up, unaware that his eyebrows were dragging on the ground.

If King Aśoka had seen him respond in such a manner at that time, he would have immediately stepped forward, placed his hand upon the elder’s forehead, and knocked his teeth three times, leaving the old venerable one with no room to exercise his supernatural powers even if he possessed them. Since he let him off then, as for what was said at the very end:
The Dragon King of Lake Anavatapta invited the Buddha for a meal. At that time, I, this poor monk, was also among their number. What do you think?
When the wind comes, the clouds rise in surging billows; when the rain clears, the thunder rolls and then subsides.
That evening’s informal discourse: Three days ago, five days later—the Buddha-dharma rests entirely in the hands of Ximufeng.
To let it go is permissible; to hold it fast is also permissible. Rolling it up or unfolding it is up to me; releasing or seizing is according to the occasion.

Dragging it upside down and sideways, piercing it through seven holes and eight apertures—just so, just so! The stray cat and the white oxen shall all testify together. How difficult, how difficult! Bi.
Yellow eyes and a yellow head are also quite coarse. Yellow myrobalan is sweet; licorice is bitter. To trigger the mechanism, one must have a crossbow capable of launching a thousand-jin bolt.
(He strikes the meditation staff once. Again, he cites: A monk asked Jingqing, “What is the source of the Great Way?
Jingqing said, “It flows forth from here. The verse says: It flows forth from here, surging on endlessly. The great waves...
Surging a thousand fathoms high—who knows there is not a single drop? Entering the hall:

When the spring light is in full bloom, all the hundred plants are beautiful and flourishing. Everywhere there is the spring breeze; in every village, the flowers and willows flourish of their own accord.
Lingyun has had a nail driven into his eyes; Xuansha reaches out from within his sleeves. Unless you yourself know how to ride backward, you shall not attain it.
A donkey: in its whole life, it never follows behind others.
When the Venerable Shu’An arrived, leaning on his staff, he ascended the hall and presented the public case of Zhaozhou visiting Zhunyu. The Master said:
This is indeed so. While murder may sometimes be excusable, irreverence is difficult to tolerate. Looking closely at this, it was Zuyou himself who invited it.

Had he been able to clench his teeth and hold his ground at that time, even if Zhaozhou had not cut off his head or severed his arms, he would still have had to go out and face the consequences himself.
Let us leave the ancients aside for a moment; as for today, when Shuai’an came to visit me, although he did not speak a word—
Probing the waters. Yet, even before one has stepped through the door, the three long and two short [measures] within the house have already been seen all at once by him.
Why? Because it is difficult to deceive those with clear eyes.
Ascending the hall, he raised [this case]: An ancient worthy said, "To speak for ten feet is not as good as practicing for one foot;
to speak for one foot is not as good as practicing for one inch. Maofeng says: I cannot speak it, nor can I practice it.
It was simply that at that time I did not act with immediate readiness; I mistakenly came from the south and, midway, broke my big toe on a stone, which still aches to this day.
The pain has still not ceased.
He ascended the hall and said: "Today marks the conclusion of the retreat. In the time of the Buddha, this was called the occasion of *pravāraṇā* (the invitation to point out faults).

Each of you practitioners should present what you have attained. Among these five hundred members of the great assembly, during these one hundred and twenty days of the summer retreat, how could there not be some areas of growth?"
"If there were one, he would have come forward to reveal it. Since everyone here keeps it secret and says nothing, let us wait to ask the staff.
He then picked up the staff and said, "Staff! You tell me: does this assembly of mine have any excellence? [The staff] says itself: 'No.
Since the assembly has no excellence, does the Elder have any excellence? [The staff] says itself:"
"No. "Since there is no point of excellence, Elder, is there perhaps no point of deficiency? "There is. "Try saying it then.
"Coarse soup and plain rice are matters of daily life; too much vinegar and too much salt will make people laugh to death."
The posthumous letter from the late Master Tian Tong Jing arrived; he ascended the hall and said: "Before Mount Taibai, the battle lines are withdrawn;
At Lake Jianhu, I sing the village field songs. Unexpectedly, the tune shifts into Xin Feng— Who would have known that this mistake is no ordinary error?"
Directly, the waters of Dong Creek flow upstream; the Milk Peak stands inverted; the Stone Woman furrows her brow; and the Wooden Man sheds tears.
With whom can this song now be heard? The mountains of Yue are boundless, and the heavens have no limit.
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said, "Three days before, five days after—if the medicine does not cause dizziness and nausea, the grievous illness will not be healed.
He struck the floor once with the staff and said, "The lame-legged Yunmen saw Muzhou."
Chongyang ascended the hall: "Today is the ninth day of the ninth month. To discuss Chan, one does not open one's mouth.

If it were Tao Yuanming, he would knit his brows and turn his head away. By the hedge, the yellow chrysanthemums are in full bloom—one branch, two branches, three branches, four, five, six, seven branches."
Ascending the hall, he said: "A single phrase—pitch black as ink. It has no handle, yet it possesses a standard. After a long silence, he asked: "Do you understand?
The pestle pounds toward the southeast; the millstone grinds toward the northwest."
Ascending the hall for the opening of the furnace: Pure and vast, bright and clear. It cannot be lifted by a ladle; it cannot be pierced by a needle.
This is so, yet you must know that the blossoming of flowers has nothing to do with spring. Take care not to let cold ashes smother you.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Seeking it a thousand times, seeking it ten thousand times, one cannot find it. Do not seek at all, and it is already manifest.
Meeting one’s father at the crossroads—eyebrows covering the eyes, a face with a beard. Heh!"
The Buddha ascends the hall after attaining enlightenment. Holding up his staff, he says: "Stars in the sky, wood upon the earth—see them as they are;

do not hesitate for a moment. Old Gautama, you needlessly rub your eyes. For twenty-one days, his mind turned back and forth; from that point on, he grasped at emptiness and then shed that very emptiness."

Poisonous venom flows everywhere through heaven and earth; it has brought misfortune to descendants down to the present day. The physician cures the deafness only to leave him blind and shaven-headed.
Although I of Mount Mao travel the same road as he, I do not stay in the same lodging. After all, how is this? He then slings his staff across his shoulder and sings:
"The crescent moon shines upon how many prefectures? With a single strike of the staff, he says: "Kuan-nai! (A single cry of the boatman).
The sounds of the mountains and waters are green.

On the first day of the New Year, he ascended the hall and held up his staff, saying: "For one full year during the old year, this old monk has been exclusively speaking empty words to you, my brothers.
By the thirtieth day of the twelfth month, not a single word proved efficacious. From this day forward, it is a new year."
I am going. I cannot help but change my voice and alter my tune; I shall speak only words of ultimate reality for all of you. *He strikes the table once.* He says:
"The horns of an ox are three feet long; the horns of a rabbit are seven inches long."
Ascending the hall on the Lantern Festival: Above and below the pavilions, fire illuminates fire; carriages and horses pass back and forth as people watch people.
Let us set aside for a moment the matter of fire illuminating fire; as for these people coming and going who can only watch others—out of ten or five pairs, not one can look at themselves.
If you all could understand how to look at yourselves, it would truly leave you with no skin to show your face. Why? Touzi said: [The text ends here.]

To the very bottom. Ascending the hall, he said: "If you intend to grasp it, you are already mistaken; if you move, you are already separated from it. Forget all artifice; cut off sound and form. With both hands, I mock and laugh at this weary exhaustion!
In the eastern village there is an old man Wang; he lets out a shout! He gave a shout.
Inviting Chief Seat Yuan to ascend the hall to ordain monks, the Master addressed the assembly, saying:
"For many years, this mountain monk has sailed a bottomless iron boat, ferrying homeless children from the south, north, east, and west, swimming within the great ocean of quiescent extinction.
At times I unfurl my sails with the current; at times I pull against the wind. Yet, in every case, I do not touch this shore."
"Reach the other shore; do not linger in midstream. However, at the point where the prow must be turned, everyone must exert their strength.

The Head Seat of the Front Hall is experienced in reading the currents and skilled in discerning the winds and clouds. Today, being right in the midst of a thousand waves and ten thousand billows, how can you allow yourselves to sit idly by?
I venture to hope that out of compassion you will extend a hand and join us in steering the vessel. Why is this? Not...
Seeing the Path. There were no idle hands on the boat.
When Master Heshang Xie Baoning arrived, he ascended the hall and said:

"Beside Phoenix Terrace, before Jade Couch Peak—whenever one stumbles or strikes against them, it is an old-world karmic enemy. Tell me, can this be avoided? Pointing toward the sky, he said: 'Heaven! Heaven!'"
Ascending the hall for the commencement of the retreat, he held up his staff and said: "The arrow has been released by the Abbot of Yuyang.

All those in this land and other realms, in the human world and the heavens, whether ordinary or holy, whether Buddhas or demons—let them all gather upon the tip of my staff to dwell in retreat and observe the precepts, collectively entering the long-term period.
Should there be any who do not obey my command, the Four Heavenly Kings shall fly hot iron [at them]."
The wheel pursues it until it arrives; once it has arrived, it has indeed arrived. What matter does this combined illumination clarify? *Zhuo!* (A sharp strike). He says:
"Seven of the Southern Dipper, eight of the Northern Dipper."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised this case: Zhaozhou said, "This old monk sets aside the two times for rice gruel and rice;
these are all matters of miscellaneous mental activity. Now tell me, apart from those two times of rice gruel and rice, where does Zhaozhou fall into error?

Even so, I of Mount Mao do not think so. When encountering rice gruel, I eat rice gruel; when encountering rice, I eat rice. What can be called "miscellaneous mental activity"? Do you understand? If...
You will also obtain it. If you can do so during the two times when you ascend to the hall, I permit you to eat gruel and rice in the company of the assembly.
If you cannot even do this, King Yama will be upon your very bowl, spoon, and chopsticks.

Please, West Hall Attendant Baoning, ascend the hall for the hanging of the plaque. A true friend of goodness (*kalyāṇamitra*) is like a great king of physicians, skillfully treating all manner of ailments.

Whether it be the sickness of the Buddhas, the sickness of the patriarchs, the sickness of the mind, the sickness of Zen, or any other ailment, he does not need to see them once to know their depth or shallowness.
Having known their depth and shallowness, he is unfailingly able to provide medicine according to the disease—what is called "strengthening the weak" and "reducing the excessive."
That which is damaged is reduced; that which is manifest on the surface is made to perspire; that which is internal is conducted out.

As for the administration of medicine, one does not distinguish between cow urine, horse fungus, croton seeds, or yellow myrobalan; all are considered wondrous medicines. They can kill, and they can also bring life.
It is evident that some can kill but cannot bring life—the dead cannot be revived by them. Others can bring life but cannot kill.

No living person can ever die. One who is skilled in these two [methods] can bring life back to those whose vital organs are exhausted and save those facing certain death, leading all people to the realm of great rest, great repose, and great peace, reaching the ground where there is no doubt.
Nevertheless, [the Master] raises his whisk and says: "Tell me, is this single pinch ultimately killing or reviving?"
"Is this *Corydalis*? Or is it *Areca nut*? West Hall Master Baoning, whose wisdom-eye is profoundly clear, is well able to distinguish between them.
We, the assembly, prostrate together and respectfully request that you deign, out of your compassion, to identify them for us."

Ascending the hall, he said: "To distinguish right from wrong and determine the difference between a grain and a penny, one must be that person. To observe the winds and clouds and discern the seasons, one must be that person.
This entire assembly here is entirely composed of such people. Pointing with his whisk, he said: "Try looking with your own eyes; can you still discern it? After a long silence, he said:
"If the morning glow does not appear at the gate, the evening glow travels a thousand miles."

Master Xie received the supervision and ascended the hall. He raised the following case: Master Zhaozhou said, "One who acts as a true spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra) must engage people with matters of their own fundamental nature.

Here at Mount Mao, I simply wish for the various manors to have bountiful harvests, so that there is plenty of gruel and rice to provide for my Zen practitioners, ensuring each one is thoroughly satiated. As for matters of the fundamental nature, I certainly do not...
I venture to raise this point. Why? Because in old age, one does not rely on physical strength for capability.
Entering the hall, [the Master said: "Before the primordial chaos was divided, it was fortunately a fine game of chess.

Without cause, Buddhas and patriarchs vied with one another to emerge, and in an instant, everything was ruined. Mount Mao has never been a master of the board; today, let me try to play it with you all."
"Look at this one move! [The Master] picks up his staff, strikes once, and says, "Wrong.
He ascends the hall, picks up his staff, and calls to the assembly: "To be hungry is to suffer from heat; to be full is to suffer from wind.
To be neither hungry nor full is precisely the disease of the vital organs (gāohuáng). This assembly of mine is certainly not among those numbers. Nevertheless, O masters..."
"Seeking well for medicine against illness.

*He strikes the desk once.* Ascending the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat: For one summer, I, Yaofeng, have spoken meaningless words to you all, yet the Old Man of Yama refused to let me off the hook and has separately prepared hell to detain me—namely, the boiling cauldrons and burning furnaces, the mountains of knives and swords.
The punishments of being bound to trees, pounded by pestles, ground by mills, plowed by oxen, and having one’s tongue torn out are twice as severe as those in the Avīci Hell.
This old monk has taken up the burden at the end; he enters into such manifold sufferings and accepts them with joy, without shrinking back. That he does not shrink back is indeed as it should be.
But will you all accept it as well? For sixty kalpas across three lifetimes.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "There is a thing, black as lacquer, spanning from antiquity to the present; no one recognizes it. Yet the autumn insects know it, chirping and sighing in vain.
Now I bring it forth for you all to examine. He then took up his staff and said: "Do you see it? Do you see it?"
He threw it down and said, "It is not worth a single coin.
He ascended the hall and said: "Everyone vies to admire the Mid-Autumn moon; only this mountain monk pays it no mind. Generally speaking, the moon in the heavens is full."
This is merely an ordinary full moon. Yet there are those who do not recognize good from evil; for no reason, they point at the moon, talk about the moon, and gaze upon the moon.

They even say, "Now is the perfect time for making offerings; now is the perfect time for practicing cultivation. With a thump on the meditation seat, they cry out, "Aha! Alas, the long night stretches on and on—when will dawn break?
Ascending the hall: Action does not stir up dust; speech does not move the lips. A ready-made commodity—gold and silver.
Have you not seen Old Dongshan? When asked about the Buddha, he answered directly: "Three pounds of flax."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Light as a goose’s down, yet heavy as a mountain; where there is no place for arrangement, one takes it up and uses it with the hand of faith.
He took up his staff and said, "Though it be a dead snake, it must be handled with life. He threw it down and said, "Grandfather!"
Ascending the hall for the opening of the furnace: In the school of the patch-robed monks, there is nothing that is not permissible. When it is hot, go everywhere to seek coolness;
when it is cold, gather around the furnace to face the fire. When hungry, eat; when weary, sleep. To grasp at dharmas and practice cultivation is like an ox pulling a millstone.
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and called to the assembly, saying: "This staff, in your own hands, crosses mountains and waters, propping up the east and propping up the west;
it functions fully through its own power. But if it comes into the hands of this mountain monk..."
It simply requires that when one wishes to stand upright, one cannot stand upright; when one wishes to lie horizontal, one cannot lie horizontal. Why? (He strikes the desk once. He says:
"In general, the monastic and the lay must be clearly distinguished."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The spring light of the second month is bright and beautiful; everywhere the flowers are in full bloom and the willows are intoxicated.
You practitioners from the five lakes and four seas must take care not to nod off with your eyes open. This entire assembly here is entirely alert and conscious.
Suddenly, picking up his staff and holding it upright, he asked, "Tell me, what is this? After a long pause, he said, "I call this a 'staff,' and then struck the ground once with it."
[The Master] descended from his seat and said: "You must not call this a 'cane' (*zhuzhangzi*). Leaning on the cane, he descended from the seat.
Upon receiving the news of the passing of Venerable Gao Yuan of Lingyin, [the Master] ascended the hall and said: "Coming, there is nowhere from which it comes—the South Peak, the North Peak.
Going, there is nowhere to which it goes—the waters of the East Ravine, the waters of the West Ravine. When illusions and bubbles suddenly vanish, one realizes that the tortoise has become a Buddha."
The white soft-shelled turtle. The pure breeze has not yet ceased. You must believe that the high plateau does not originally die. Since it does not die, tell me:
where is it? Holding up his staff, he says: "Do you see? Do you see? He strikes once and says: "If you recognize it, it remains as before—no longer the same."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "It cannot be named; it cannot be described. What thing, then, is it? If you can see it, you will use it intimately, not depending on another.
Sometimes it is so; sometimes it is not so. A featherless hawk flies close to the sky;
a horned tiger lies across the road."

Ascending the hall, he said: "Where there is light, there must be darkness; where there is darkness, there must be light. To speak with the mouth is like being mute; to see with the eyes is like being blind. Ultimately, how is it?
Outside the gate lies a single postal road, upon which people travel morning and night."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Xuansha did not cross the ridge; Baoshou did not wade across the river. Gaoting saw a beckoning hand and ran straight toward it;
Zifu saw the flagpole and turned back immediately. These four fellows were all short by one point. Why?
Because if a person lacks far-reaching foresight, they will surely have immediate troubles."
On the anniversary of the passing of Master Po’an, he offered incense and said: "In the blazing heat of the sixth month, whirlwinds scatter snow.
Baizhang went deaf; Huangbo stuck out his tongue. The sea is vast and the mountains high—who can discuss this? Every time one drinks water, one chokes."
Ascending the hall: "The ninth day—this very morning is it. Who knows whether it is so or not?
If you say it is not, Yuanming took up his wine and ascended the eastern heights. If you say it is, the destitute son lies naked upon the dewy ground.
Reaching this point, often ten or five pairs of people have reason but no way to clear themselves. Now, let this staff speak out for all of you. [He strikes the staff.]
A moment’s pause. Opening the furnace, he ascends the hall: "Gautama, you are Gautama; Bodhidharma comes from another Bodhidharma. There is some deliberation regarding the Buddha-dharma;
each of you return to your quarters and warm yourselves by the fire. Although this is so, you must still take care of your eyebrows.
Entering the city and departing the camp, he ascended the hall. He addressed the assembly, saying:

"All of you sitting and standing here before me, solemnly gazing at one another, eye to eye—none of you can deceive this mountain monk by even a single point, nor can this mountain monk deceive you by even a single point.
Nevertheless, you must know there is a phrase for mutually deceiving one another. If such exists, try to bring it forth."
"Look! If there is no one [who can see], this mountain monk cannot help but emulate the majestic deportment of the Seven Buddhas;
I shall ride backward upon the Buddha Hall and pass through the nostrils of you all."
Emerging from the assembly hall and returning to the Dharma Hall, he held up his staff and called to the great assembly, saying: "Half real and half false, it is the merchandise of a thousand houses;
neither real nor unreal, it is a treasure casket of a hundred jewels. He struck the ground once and said: "Opened completely, everything is seen.
Who is there to divide the spoils by fire? Leaning on the staff, he said: "One portion I offer to Śākyamuni Buddha; one portion I offer to..."
At the Precious Buddha Stupa, he ascended the hall. Holding up his staff, he called to the assembly, saying: "Some people, upon seeing this staff, call it a staff;
some people, upon seeing this staff, do not call it a staff. Yet, in either case, there is no connection to the truth. Do you understand? (2)"
Because of the one existence, even that one is not to be clung to. When the single mind does not arise, the myriad dharmas are without fault.
[The Master] threw down his staff and said, "The Third Patriarch, the Great Master, has arrived!"
Ascending the hall, he said: "The samādhi of the present before us has no front or back. Snow weighs down the pavilions; the wind howls through the pines and cypresses.
I recall how in the past, Shuilao was kicked over by Mazu with a single step. Upon rising, he could not help but cry out:
'I have recognized the source right upon the tip of a single hair! Aha-ha! He makes even the foolish Bagua of Mingzhou laugh to tears."

On the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month, during a snowfall, he ascended the hall. Addressing the assembly, he said: "The Yellow-Faced Gautama once went to the Snow Mountains and practiced austerities for six years.

At night, beholding the morning star, he suddenly awakened to the Way. Thereupon, for twenty-one days, he contemplated such matters until he reached a point where there was no place to open his mouth.
This was not unique to Gautama; even as I, [the Master], contemplate this on Mount Mao, there is likewise no opening."

[The Master] said, "In the place of the mouth. Nevertheless, matters are not univocal; one must reveal some news. After a long silence, he said, "Do you understand? This is the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month.
Looking back at the snow on the Snowy Mountains, it falls thickly before Mount Mao; it has never been of two different colors."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Of the three hundred and sixty days of a year, look at them—soon they will all be spent.
Thus it is said: 'As this day passes, life also diminishes accordingly; like a fish in scant water, what joy can there be? It is also said:

'One should be diligent and energetic, as if putting out a fire on one's own head. Everyone, try to examine yourselves with fierce mindfulness: is this joy, or is it not? If you have not yet attained that joy,"
You must act as if your head were on fire. Even if you find it pleasant to go, you must still act as if your head were on fire. Why?
Tianshu Nu, have you not heard it said: "If one studies, [the learning] will not be firm"?
The Abbot ascends the hall to take his place at the head of the assembly. The establishment of the monastic order’s governance values the securing of the right person;

it is much like the state’s investiture of a general, which requires one who is fully equipped with both civil and military virtues, possessing both strategic wisdom and tactical skill, and who has the hand capable of rescuing from peril and supporting those in distress.
Only then can one overcome the world, such that all are swept along like grass bending before the wind. My teaching is likewise similar to this:
it requires that the elbows and arms be heavy, and the claws and fangs be sharp. Without sharpness, one cannot break through the gates of humanity and heaven;
without weight, one cannot weigh the Buddhas and Patriarchs. When these two qualities are possessed, the monastic communities will flourish. The monastic communities...
Having already stirred them, what further matter is there to clarify? After a long silence, Lu Zu faced the wall; Xuefeng rolled the ball.
On the night of the Lantern Festival, the Head Seat was invited to ascend the hall to ordain monks: "A towering phrase prior to sound; a vast mechanism beyond measure.

If you have not yet clarified the three eights and nine, it will be difficult to discern the 'encircled power' and the 'rare. If you can discern and clarify this, you shall see the succession of the patriarchs."
This has been transmitted from one to another, with the lamps continuing one after another until the present day; the true wind has not fallen.
Should this not yet be so, the head seat of this hall is deeply versed in this principle. Each of you should take him as your teacher and draw near to him; strike upon him and question him.
Do not wait until old age before returning empty-handed.

Ascending the hall, he struck the meditation staff and said: "Internal emptiness, external emptiness, internal-and-external emptiness. The four great elements and the five aggregates cannot be apprehended;
mountains, rivers, and the great earth cannot be apprehended. Even that which cannot be apprehended cannot itself be apprehended.
He struck once more and said: "The god Śūnyatā has a black face."
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and said: "This staff is difficult to grasp. At times it is joyful; at times it is fierce.
It stirs the vast ocean and pierces through the azure void. He struck once and said: "How does this compare to Puhua shaking his bell?"
Ascending the hall, he said: "Before form and name have manifested, the patterns and colors are fully revealed. The short remains short; the long remains long.
Gautama of Yellow Face needlessly speaks of yellow roads and black paths; why must Bodhidharma with the beard travel through Wei and Liang?
Striking the meditation seat, he said: 'I long remember the second and third months in Jiangnan; where the partridges cry, the hundred flowers are fragrant.'"
Ascending the hall: The three months of spring are nearly spent; Ten thousand trees present their verdant tips. A light rain wets the lingering red petals;
The sound of the spring blends with the cries of hidden birds. How pitiable! How laughable! Hanshanzi returns, yet cannot find his way back; He has forgotten the path by which he came.
Ascending the hall, he took up his staff, struck it once, and said, "Deshan did not understand.
He gave a shout and said, "Linji did not know. Where do you all meet with Yuyang? Again he struck it once and followed with two shouts.
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff, called to the assembly, and struck it once. He said: "The Buddha-lands of worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges are utterly pulverized;
Śākyamuni and Maitreya gulp down their breath and swallow their voices. As for all other Buddhas and patriarchs, where else could they even find a place to vent their frustration?
Nevertheless, though this is so, it does not accord with the essential school."
Ascending the hall on the Double Fifth Festival: The entire earth is medicine; there is nothing that is not medicine.

Picking it up with the hand as it comes, every single thing is beyond grasping or rejecting. Holding up his staff, he asked, "What medicine is this? He struck the ground once and said, "The pill for all ailments."
When Master Yì of Xinzhimén arrived, the Master ascended the hall and said: "A monk asked Zhimén, 'What is it like when the lotus flower has not yet emerged from the water?
Zhimén said, 'The lotus flower. The monk asked, 'What is it like after it has emerged? Zhimén said, 'The lotus leaf. The Master said: 'One is direct; the other is circuitous.
If a patch-robed monk understands this, he is merely adding grit to his eyes. If it were I, Wùyuáng, however, I would say..."
However, there was a question: "What is it like when the lotus has not yet emerged from the water? [The Master replied: "A lotus leaf. "What is it like after it has emerged from the water?
[The Master replied: "A lotus flower. Now tell me, is there any distinction of superiority or inferiority between this and Zhimen? A monk from Sichuan is coarse; a monk from Zhejiang is elegant.
Ascending the hall, he called to the assembly, saying: "In ancient times, the ancients set a ninety-day period for the summer retreat to realize enlightenment.
Now, in the blink of an eye, midsummer has already passed. As for the matter within each of you, what is it? Is there something realized, or is there nothing realized?
Setting aside for a moment the case of having something realized—now only midsummer remains—and yet you have not yet realized anything."
The bottom! You must quickly realize it. But what is it that you should realize? "The lotus leaves are round and round like mirrors;
the water chestnut tips are sharp and sharp like awls. The wind blows the willow catkins like flying balls; the rain beats the pear blossoms as butterflies fly."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Three parts of time have already passed; two are gone. How is it that the single point of the numinous platform remains unpolished?
Indeed, even in the act of defecating and urinating, there is no room for anything else. Greedily pursuing life, one wanders about in petty toil day after day.

Like Fan Kuai at the Red Gate—once he has stepped forward, he cannot be called back; what can be done about such a struggle? It is either south of the Yellow River or north of it. Today, Yewang [the Master]..."
The nostrils are in the hands of everyone; they may be dragged this way or that as they please.
On the occasion of the Mid-Autumn Festival, he ascended the hall: "The myriad sounds are hushed; the empty hall is silent at night.
I do not see Master Hanshan, yet I cannot help but remember him in vain. Do not remember him! He then raised his whisk and said, "It turns out he has been right here with you all along."
"Let us enjoy the Mid-Autumn Festival together. [The Master] then spoke ill of the ways of small families:
"My mind is like the autumn moon; it is as clear and bright as a deep pool. Nothing can be compared to it. How am I to describe it?
It has been described, yet why do you all see as if not seeing and hear as if not hearing? He struck the meditation seat and said, "How remarkably alert!"
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The ancients said: 'Those who enter through the gate of Mañjuśrī find the triggering of their potential in walls, bricks, and rubble.
Those who enter through the gate of Avalokiteśvara find the triggering of their potential in frogs and earthworms. Those who enter through the gate of Samantabhadra arrive without moving a step.
Nevertheless, though the new moon has its night of fullness, the human heart never knows when it is satisfied."
Ascending the hall: This morning is the twenty-fifth day of the eighth month. I recall Dongshan departing at Chadu; at the peak of Mount Shaoshi, he was struck and would not turn back.
To this very day, he has had no fundamental basis. When asked about the Buddha, he replied with "three pounds of flax.
How does that compare to the cypress tree in the courtyard? Do you understand? A hawk seizes a prostrate hare; a cat catches a rat.

Ascending the hall, he said: "The myriad pipes of nature sigh with melancholy; dewdrops fall from the thousand forests. Wild geese rise from the level sands; night insects chirp through the broken walls.

To raise one, you may not raise two; let this one move pass. [He] suddenly grasps his staff and says: "Listen further as this staff reveals a message. He strikes once.* *Note: The final strike of the staff is a traditional Zen gesture signifying the direct transmission of the Dharma beyond words and concepts. It serves here as the ultimate "message" of the staff itself. The preceding instructions—“raise one but not two” and “let this one move pass”—are classic Zen pedagogical devices intended to cut off dualistic thinking and point toward immediate, non-conceptual realization.*
Ascending the hall, he called to the assembly, saying: "There is no Way to study; there is no Chan to investigate. Those with yellow heads and blue eyes merely talk of pointing south.
The mist clears and the clouds disperse as the heavens open wide; before the gate there are fortunately a thousand peaks of green, ten thousand peaks of green.
One wanders about until one wins the chance to lean against the railing."
Ascending the hall, he said: "Regarding this matter, if you people do not know it, then let it be; you need not concern yourselves with it.
But if you do know it and wish to understand it, it is truly a calamity that kills one, for there is no place where it can be understood.
Why? Because if you people intend to seek it in the east, it is certainly not in the east; if you intend to search for it in the west, it is certainly not in the west. You people..."
One simply wishes to let go with firm resolve and pay no mind to it at all; yet, it is as if one were facing an enemy from a previous life, unable to escape or be rid of it.
At such a time, how can one ultimately proceed? [The Master] raises his whisk and says: "Enemy! Enemy!"
The Chief Seat Xie took up the whisk and ascended the hall for the formal discourse. Speaking horizontally or vertically, when has he ever moved his tongue?
Acting in reverse or acting in accord, it is all merely the everyday meal. Having its own standard yet no boundaries—[the Master] drew a line with the whisk and said:
Do you understand? My Way is one that runs through all things.

On the Winter Solstice, he ascended the hall, took up his staff, and called to the assembly, saying: "The first yang has arisen; the myriad species have arisen. It is precisely at this moment of arising."
"How is it? [The Master] strikes once and says: "The myriad shadows vanish; my Way flourishes greatly. Ascending the hall, he cites a case:
A monk asked Puzhi, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West? Puzhi said, "A cluster of bamboo before the courtyard does not grow cold on its own despite the frost.
After all, how is it? One hears only the sound of the wind striking it; one knows it must be several thousand [stems].
[The Master] held up the staff and said, "Do you all understand? If you do understand, you will see the principle of the direct pointing of the School Gate.
If you still do not understand, I, Yuyang, shall provide a verse for you. He then recited the previous verse and descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall: There are twelve months in a year; this month is now coming to an end.
There are thirty days in a month; this day is just beginning. This day is simply an ordinary day—where is the place where it begins?
This month is simply an ordinary month—where is the place where it ends? If you can apply a single eye here, I grant that you all understand.
Regarding the meaning of non-transmigration: if this were not so, arising and ceasing would never cease; every thought-moment would pass away and shift.
When you reach the thirtieth day, the Old Man Yama will demand payment for your meal-money. Do not say that I did not warn you.

Ascending the hall on the eighth day of the twelfth lunar month: Two thousand years ago, the Old Man with the Yellow Face beheld the morning star before Mount Vimalasvabhāva one night and suddenly awakened to the Way.
For twenty-one days thereafter, he contemplated this matter; truly, there was no place for him to open his mouth.
This matter is so vividly manifest that it cannot be presented to others; it cannot be explained to others. Only those who have realized it for themselves can know it.
Now, as for this matter of realization—how is it? Have you not seen what Master Zhenjing said: "The Dhūta Rock is enveloped by moss;
Peak of Thrown Pens is entwined by *bìlì* vines; in Luohan Monastery, three are ordained every year."
"Practitioners, you may go to Guizong Temple to attend the formal session and drink tea. Today, I have no leisure to drink tea with everyone;
let us descend from the seat together to the Miaosheng Hall to offer incense and pay our respects. However, at the place where we prostrate, each of you must take care.
But what exactly are you taking care of? Do not let yourselves strike your foreheads and break them."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The phrase prior to sound; the capacity beyond measure. Bright and vivid; steep and towering. Those who raise it are few, and those who see it are rare.
Holding up the corner of his *kāṣāya*, he asked, "Do you see? Do you see? He shook out his many years of worn-out patchwork robe:
"Tattered and frayed, half of it flies away with the clouds."
Ascending the hall on the occasion of the Festival of Scattering Flowers: Vast is space; vast is the Sage’s mind. Boundless is space; boundless is the Sage’s virtue.
With boundless virtue, he covers both the Chinese and the barbarians; with a vast mind, he encompasses heaven and earth.
Encompassing heaven and earth, his mind becomes ever more luminous; extending to both the civilized and the barbarian, his virtue renews itself daily.
It endures long and continuous, vast and beyond naming. At such a time as this, what is it like? The village elder knows nothing of the labors of Yao and Shun;
drum beats thump-thump as they sacrifice to the River God.
The Abbot ascends the hall on the first day of the first month. Today is the festival of the Lantern Festival.

Whether in the bustling markets of the red dust, at wine shops, or within flower grottoes, lanterns are lit everywhere. Princes and noblemen crowd together in their carriages and horses, coming and going to view the sights;
even the poets and scholars exchange verses in long and short lines—all of them take the lantern as an occasion for Buddhist practice. As it is said:
One lamp ignites a hundred thousand lamps; the lamps continue one after another. One phrase unfolds into ten trillion phrases;
every phrase returns to the source. Although it is thus, tell me: before the single lamp has been lit and before the single phrase has taken form, how can one realize this?
After a long silence, he said: "It would be better to cut out one's tongue than to violate the taboo names of the state.
[On the occasion of] the Buddha’s Nirvana, he ascended the hall and said: "The old fellow with the yellow face sells his idle trinkets; he is the Great King of Physicians for the world."
Who would have known that amidst so much illness, when his strength was exhausted and his schemes were spent, he still rubbed his chest and addressed the assembly, saying:
"Those who say I have entered parinirvāṇa are not my disciples; those who say I have not entered parinirvāṇa are likewise not my disciples.
He then turned to look at the great assembly and asked, "Do you understand? A chicken of Chu is no phoenix from Mount Dan."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The spring breeze sweeps vast; the spring rain falls incessantly. Flowers gather the morning dew; willows bear the cold mist.
Transformation acts without acting; the myriad dharmas are so without being so. Bodhidharma sat facing the wall for nine years in vain;
Sudhana ran until his skin was worn through."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Under the heels of every person there is a patch of ground the size of a sitting mat.

Today, this mountain monk likewise does not dare to move even a single hair’s breadth, nor do I wish for you all to move even a single hair’s breadth. Grasp it directly! I ask the assembly: Can you grasp it?"
"Ma. After a long silence, he said, "Moss has grown.
He ascended the hall and said: "Hearing shallowly yet awakening deeply; hearing deeply yet not awakening. Meeting Bodhidharma while lost—Zhaozhou sips vinegar."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Fire exists within wood; only when drilled does it become manifest. Gold exists within ore; only when smelted does it become refined.
Within each of you there is a priceless treasure. Why do you willingly allow yourselves to sink into the pit of the sense-spheres (*āyatana*)?
The pit of the sense-spheres!"—he struck the meditation staff once and said, "It is shattered! But where is the treasure? He then threw [the staff].

This person deserves thirty blows. Why? Because they have not seen the Way: "To regulate them with ritual. Entering the hall:
More than half of this summer retreat has already passed. Often, those who were diligent become indolent. Fortunately, this matter is fully and naturally present;

Nanquan, how is he compared to Xuefeng’s visiting Old Guan?
On the anniversary of Master Po’an’s passing, I offer incense: "In the past, before I had set out on my travels, I already knew that the nostrils were upon the face;
yet after wandering through various quarters, they remain exactly as they were, without shifting by so much as a single hair’s breadth. Fortunately," [he continues].
How pitiful! Without cause, he lost his footing and came before this old, frozen fellow.

Ascending the hall: "Alala! It stretches across everything. How high is heaven? How vast is earth? The blue-eyed one and the yellow-headed one merely bicker and clamor among themselves.
When Yuyang speaks thus, it is like using salt to quench thirst."
Master Xie Jianshou ascends the hall: When one point is penetrated, every point is penetrated; the hand is nimble and the feet are agile.
I always remember Nanquan’s raising of it: "The sickle for cutting grain is as swift as the wind."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] looked up at the sky and lowered his head to gaze at the earth. "What point is there for a monk with clear eyes to seek?
he asked. "Have you not seen that in Mingjue Temple before the mountain, there is a Dharma teacher Chen who can say:

Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The ancients said: 'It is like a wild goose passing through the vast sky; its shadow sinks into the cold water.

The goose has no intention of leaving a trace, and the water has no thought of receiving the shadow. At this very moment, it cannot be grasped, nor can it be abandoned. Within that which cannot be attained, one simply attains it.

Ashamed of having no money. Ascending the hall on the Mid-Autumn Festival: The month before was this very same moon; the month after will also be this very same moon. Why then do worldly people vie to celebrate the Mid-Autumn Festival?
It is not that they do not vie in celebration; but tell me, what is the matter within the Palace of Broad Cold (Guanghan Gong)? Good!
A long time ago, it is said: "Where did Nanquan’s sweeping of his sleeves go? Yaoyao’s parting of the clouds left him unable to stop laughing. He ascended the hall and said:

Later, however, at Dayu’s place, he received three punches under the ribs. This is what is meant by 'the furnace and bellows, where even dull iron is refined.'"
Much indeed. When Deshan came out from the gorges, his spirit swallowed the universe; yet upon reaching Longtan, he blew out the paper candle and lost his nostrils.
He then took all his commentaries and sub-commentaries and burned them at once, saying: "To exhaust all profound dialectics is like placing a single hair in the great void;
to exhaust all worldly mechanisms is like casting a single drop into a vast abyss. Even so, it still remains somewhat pedantic—this was said regarding Linji.
Setting aside Deshan for a moment, tell me: in what place does Yuyang manifest as a person? After a long silence, he said: "By day one sees the sun; by night one sees the stars.
On the Double Ninth, he ascended the hall, took up his staff, and said: "The ninth day is a fine festival; yellow chrysanthemums are fresh everywhere. Meeting [you all]..."
"Many are guests intoxicated by wine; few are seen who remain sober alone. *He strikes once* and says, "To strike the grass is only to startle the snake.
Ascending the hall, he held up his staff and showed it to the assembly, saying: "At the very moment of seeing, that which sees is not the seeing. Even seeing is already apart from seeing."
It cannot be reached by seeing. Furthermore, how can one realize that which is beyond the reach of seeing? *He strikes once* and says:
"The monks' hall sees through the kitchen of Fragrant Accumulation; the *chīwén* dragon-head gargoyle bites off the ridge of the Buddha Hall."
Ascending the hall, he raised his whisk and addressed the assembly, saying: "This very thing is it; there is nothing beyond this.
Those who follow me shall go south or north with me; those who do not follow me shall remain deadlocked in the east or west.
If you all stubbornly refuse to believe, five days from now you will run into your own father at the crossroads. Do not say that I, Yuyang, did not tell you today."
Ascending the hall: Before the Seven Buddhas, where there was no news, there was news; who does not know this? After the Seven Buddhas, where there was news, there was no news;
such people do not understand. Whether one knows or not, whether one understands or not—it is uncut jade and unrefined gold, a lump of clay and a clod of earth.
When the Venerable Master Daci Xiaoweng arrived, he ascended the hall and said: "If you wish to clarify this matter, you must encounter the right person.
Once you have encountered the right person, naturally eye will meet eye and mind will recognize mind—like gold being traded for gold, or water merging with water.
Have you not seen how one day, while Daci was sweeping the floor, Zhaozhou asked him: 'In what does Prajñā consist?'"

Daci asked, "What is the essence of Prajñā? Zhaozhou laughed heartily. The next day, while Zhaozhou was sweeping the floor, Daci again asked, "What is the essence of Prajñā? Zhaozhou set down his broom and once more laughed heartily.
Daci then went straight to the abbot’s quarters. After the Master had finished recounting this, he laughed heartily and said, "These two..."
This old fellow—looking at it with cold eyes, it is indeed laughable. It will take thirty years before one truly laughs. Why?
Because I thought the world was red with beards, yet who would have known there were also red-bearded barbarians?
Ascending the hall on the Winter Solstice: When the six yin lines are completely stripped away, one must not linger; when the single yang line is reborn, it is difficult to conceal.
In that which is difficult to conceal, every thing is already perfected; in that moment of non-lagging, every particle of dust is liberated. (Raising his staff, he said:)
"This very thing—how could it not be manifest? *Zhuo!* (He strikes the desk. How could one not be liberated?
If you can understand it thus, I grant that all of you have realized the stage of non-retrogression. If it is otherwise, then count from the beginning: one-nine, two-nine, three-nine, four-nine;
there is still much freezing cold ahead."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "In one year there are twelve months; now only this one month remains. At the very end of this month, one sees the months of the coming year again.
Since this cycle has no beginning, why labor over forced distinctions? When distinctions do not arise, the limits of before and after are severed.
When the limits of before and after are severed, true wisdom manifests. When true wisdom manifests, one does not perceive anything as manifesting."
Nor does one form a conceptual understanding of it as something not manifest before one. At such a time, how is it?
Have you not seen Langye’s praise of Bodhidharma, which says: "The Master’s mind wears [the sky] upon its head"?
Ascending the hall: Brocade wrapping a special stone; iron encasing a lump of clay. A living livelihood; a dialect beyond the ordinary.
An enlightened-eyed monk cannot comprehend it: the moon shifts its reflection upon the plum blossoms on the railing.
Ascending the hall on the first day of the year: "Today is the first day of the first month. We must seize the moment.

Ascending the hall on the occasion of the Festival of Scattering Heavenly Flowers: To speak sufficiently is to spend the entire day speaking and yet exhaust the Way;

After a long silence, he said: "The peach on Mount Pan bears fruit only once every three thousand years; may Your Majesty’s sagely calculations extend for hundreds of millions of springs.

There was another person who, upon hearing these words, slandered them with the mind of an icchantika. I say that such a person is alive and already trapped in hell.
Now tell me, which of these two can be saved? Do you understand? Three before and three after; ten pairs and five singles.
Warmth in the south of the Yangtze; bitter cold in the north of the Great Wall.

In this world of purity and peace, there is no idle place.

The Abbot Xie held a summer retreat feast. The Head Seat took up the whisk and ascended the hall. He called to the assembly, saying:

[Zhaozhou] said, "I have attained it. [Linji] said, "This satiety does not depart. Being obstructed by satiety, it is merely empty satiety; it is not true satiety. Zhang said, "I am just like this;

All attained the joy of Dharma-bliss and the delight of dhyāna. Zhang said, "Though it is joyful, one must forget this joy before it can be attained.
If this joy is not forgotten, one is constrained by joy; that is not true joy. Thus the two men questioned and debated with one another.

"I also know this. But tell me, when I, the mountain monk, pinched their hands at that time and the two of them departed in shame, what was your intention?

planting green pines by the road."

Ascending the hall on the Dragon Boat Festival: Entering a field of weeds, one does not pick; whatever is grasped by the hand is none other than medicine.

Even if every person throughout the entire world were to fall ill, each with a different ailment, upon reaching this place of Yuyang, they need take but a single dose, and all shall be made to cast off their sickness.

He struck it again and said, "I grant you one more dose."
Ascending the hall: Five times five is twenty-five; six times six is thirty-six. Even with the Great Divination (Dayan) numbers, in the end they are still insufficient.
If the numbers were sufficient, there would be no insufficiency. Blue-eyed and yellow-headed, their mouths are mute and their tongues are bald.

this resentment cannot be washed away. Oṃ pèn pèn fa fa chì shè."
Ascending the hall: Morning bustle, evening leisure—neither indolence nor diligent cultivation. After all, what is it?
The Boatman of Huating; Zhaozhou of the Northland.
Ascending the hall upon the conclusion of the retreat: "The ninety days are now complete; how has that matter fared? Those who dwell in non-action and non-affairs often fall into negligence.
I, Yuyang, dare say they do not fall into negligence. Why? Because in their youth, they once broke through the battle lines of dragons and snakes."
An old man singing just like a young child.

Striking the meditation bench, he said: "As expected."

Holding up the imperial edict: From the very beginning, there has been nothing more highly esteemed than this one point. It reaches the state where transformation occurs without words and harmony is achieved without concert;

4. On the summit of a solitary peak, one howls at the moon and sleeps amidst the clouds; this is unmistakably selfless and possesses a clear basis in every instance.

To this very day, it remains unrecoverable. Nevertheless, were it not for the path of the woodcutter, how could one have reached this place?"

It cannot be done this way; it cannot be done that way. With a single flip of the body, one strides across the great void. Only—
This spiritual blade—dare anyone attempt to match it? It can release and it can seize; it can kill and it can bring back to life. It knows neither high nor low; it has no factions and no partiality.
It leaves no trace in any place, yet it achieves perfection in every place. [The Master] pats the meditation seat and says: "I know not who in this world understands this;
let us together support this broken-legged cauldron. He then raises the case of Sansheng asking Xuefeng about "penetrating through."
Regarding the public case: “The golden-scaled fish in the net—what do you take for food? [The Master] picks it up and says: “The soft cannot withstand the hard;
the hard cannot withstand the soft. Nevertheless, even though this is so, when examined closely, one cannot avoid having both gain and loss.
Let those with eyes discern this!”
After thanking the two classes of officials and welcoming the Abbot of the Wanyan West Hall, he ascended the hall and said:

The Wheel of the Dharma: Just as the hundred rivers rush toward the sea, all returning to a single flavor, so it is with me, this mountain monk, who have newly come to reside at Mount Jing.

each has extended a hand to establish this protective community and uphold the True Lineage. Yet, in the midst of this, you must first of all not recognize me.
I do not know you; we do not reflect one another. Each is unaware of the other. If you are joyful, I am not willing.
Tell me, why is it so? When righteousness emerges, there is a bountiful year.
On the Double Ninth Festival, Chongyang ascended the hall. He called to the assembly, saying: "The end of last year, the end of this year—do not let the next year follow after that.
Year after year it is just like this. The chrysanthemums bloom profusely as we grow drunk on the Double Ninth; the fallen leaves rustle mournfully, filling the earth with sorrow."
"Do you all understand? [With the whisk, he strikes the meditation seat and says: 'I have nothing hidden from you.
He ascends the hall for the opening of the furnace. A monk asks: "The season of early winter presses on once more; throughout the vast lands, the furnaces and bellows are opened."
"Only at Mount Jing do we have the 'gentle and fierce fire. I wonder how many people it has roasted alive.

The Master said, "Bury them all in one pit. [The student] said, "It may be so..."
"It is like striking a scorched brick that hits one right on the frozen bottom; it is like a red-eyed man bumping into a firebrand.

Upon returning home from his travels, he ascended the hall and said: "If we discuss this matter, it is like a nation dispatching an army. There must be capable men both in the vanguard and in the rear.

"A thousand li. Then, in battle there is nothing that is not victorious; in attack there is nothing that is not taken. Moreover, having played the victory tune and turned the spearhead back, one halts the reins and finds joy for oneself—how do you say it in a single phrase?
'The bow is broken, the horse released; there is no further business. Leaning on my staff, I encounter spring; I mark the extraordinary flowers. He spoke again:

When the Venerable Master Heiyuan Tiantong arrived, he ascended the hall and said: "Sharing the same body and the same life; sharing the same breath and connected by the same branch.

In front of you all, let it bite sideways or vertically as it pleases. If there is even one or half a person who can bite through it and pass beyond it, then the peaks of the breasts and the nostrils will all be in your hands; let me hear you drag it sideways and pull it upside down.
If you cannot bite through it, then your nostrils will instead be in the hands of this mountain monk. For the ninety days of this summer retreat, I shall go...
One cannot go; yet one cannot stay when required to stay. At such a moment as this, how does one find a way to breathe out?
[He strikes the meditation staff once. He says: "Cloudless, clouds arise upon the ridge; the moon exists, yet it sets in the heart of the waves."
Small-scale Sermon upon the Resolution of the Summer Retreat. The assembly at Lufeng possesses the nature of great icchantikas. What, indeed, was accomplished during these ninety days of summer?
This refers to the "binding" on the fifteenth day of the fourth month. We have dwelt together in the five realms of uninterrupted hell, sporting at all times.

Upon mountains of knives and trees of swords, we are pounded by pestles and ground by millstones; from our open mouths, nothing but black smoke is spat forth, and every movement of thought is nothing other than evil.
Reflect: when evil thoughts arise, they fill the void of space; even the entire extent of empty space cannot contain them.

This is like the release on the fifteenth day of the seventh month. Once evil karma is fully accumulated, one realizes the body of a Māra king, never to be lost again for as long as the future endures.
Thus, you see that the assembly before you has truly not spent this summer in vain. You see the assembly before you...
Since it does not pass away in vain, neither the lanterns nor the weathered pillars pass away in vain.
Neither the mountains, rivers, and great earth, nor the grasses, trees, and forests, nor sentient and insentient beings—all do not pass away in vain. Even this staff does not pass away in vain.
Since the staff does not pass away in vain, tell me: what has been accomplished? It is a whole body of black lacquer, a coarse thorny jujube—far from being merely...
Climbing mountains while simultaneously striking dogs.
A small *sōsan* (informal discourse) on a winter night: The Buddhas of the past have closed the void and locked the dream; the Buddhas of the present entrust their hats to the river.

The Buddhas of the future will be like those who hope to quench their thirst by looking at a plum. Great assembly, from ancient times until now, the sun and moon, the mountains and rivers, human relations, and the seasonal festivals have remained as they are.
Each of you here, with teeth intact and hair upon your heads, must above all not allow yourselves to be deceived.
Nowadays there are a certain kind of people who, as soon as they hear even a slight mention of this, immediately accept it here in a casual and superficial manner.
It must be so; it is certain that one must go, and it is fitting that one must go. For now, we only know that mid-winter is severe cold and early summer is gradually warming;
yet we fail to realize that early summer is gradually warming and mid-winter is severe cold. When Lurong makes this announcement, tell me:

is he deceiving others and deceiving himself, or does he have some other superior quality? After a long silence, he said: "To pour out one's heart and expose one's liver—there is no one [to hear it]."
[The Master] said: "To pull out the tongue and plow with it—only one knows this oneself.
At the small *cán* (lecture) marking the conclusion of the retreat, he held up his staff and addressed the assembly, saying: "Look! Look!

Whether sages or ordinary beings, whether sentient or insentient, throughout the ten directions of the world, all dwell and enter the retreat here. For the ninety days of this summer, today [they] announce..."
The end. The Dharma-gates attained therein and the practices and vows cultivated are each different.
As for the Buddhas, they are fully endowed with the knowledge of all modes (*sarvākārajñatā*). As for the Bodhisattvas, they have accomplished the gates of the *pāramitās*.

As for the rest—the learners (*śaikṣa*) and those beyond learning (*aśaikṣa*)—this lot of incompetent fellows, let them be set aside and not discussed. But consider, for instance, this assembly before us.
I have spent this summer with this mountain monk, our eyebrows knotted together and our teeth clattering against one another. Tell me, is there anything gained here?
